title: Nvidia Probes Huang Ties as AI Industry Weighs the Fallout
content:
Nvidia is moving to contain the fallout from an investigation into whether its CEO, Jensen Huang, was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. But the controversy raises a larger question for an AI industry that has become deeply dependent on the company – and the executive who has spent three decades building it.
Nvidia’s board said on November 8 that it had launched an independent investigation after reports linked Huang to a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed International, who US authorities reportedly suspected of working for China. A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside counsel, will oversee the inquiry.
The board said it had no reason to believe US national security or Nvidia’s proprietary information had been compromised. Huang supports the investigation and has committed to cooperating, the company said.
Huang separately acknowledged in a
message to employees
that he had been unfaithful to his wife and apologized to his family, colleagues and shareholders. He said he remained fully committed to Nvidia, to protecting the company, and to supporting US national security.
Related:
AMD Launches Epyc SP7, Helion as AI Rack Demand Rises
A company spokesperson sought to head off questions about a possible leadership disruption. “Today’s news will not slow Nvidia. Jensen is committed to continuing to lead Nvidia as CEO without interruption,” spokesperson John Rizzo said, according to the Associated Press.
The immediate issue is whether the investigation finds evidence that Huang’s relationship created a national security or corporate security risk. The longer-term question is what happens to Nvidia – and the AI infrastructure market built around its technology – if its longtime CEO can no longer lead the company.
Huang, who co-founded Nvidia in 1993, has led the company through its transformation from a graphics processor maker into the dominant supplier of accelerators for training and running AI models. His influence extends well beyond chip design. Huang has become the industry’s most recognizable advocate for accelerated computing, promoting an integrated Nvidia platform that spans GPUs, networking, software, and complete data center systems.
His position gives him an unusually prominent role in the investment cycle surrounding AI infrastructure. Hyperscalers, cloud providers and AI developers are making multiyear commitments to Nvidia technology. Those decisions influence data center construction, power procurement, cooling systems, networking deployments, and semiconductor manufacturing capacity.
Related:
Google Adds TPU 8tx, 8i Max for Enterprise AI
A change in leadership would not automatically disrupt those commitments. Nvidia has an established engineering organization, manufacturing relationships, and a large executive team. Its customers also have substantial investments in the company’s software and hardware ecosystem.
But replacing Huang could introduce uncertainty around the company’s strategic direction and its relationships with major customers and suppliers.
Nvidia’s Relationships Could Be Harder to Replace
Huang’s influence over Nvidia’s business extends beyond his role as CEO, according to Steven Dickens, CEO and principal analyst at HyperFrame Research. His relationships with senior executives across the technology industry have developed over decades and would be difficult for another executive to replicate, he said.
“Those relationships are based on decades,” Dickens said, citing Huang’s connections with Dell Technologies CEO Michael Dell and executives at major hyperscalers. Dickens said he has witnessed Huang’s interactions with senior technology executives and heard how those executives discuss him in private meetings.
“His relationships with those senior leaders are ridiculously hard to replicate,” he said.
Those relationships have commercial value for Nvidia, Dickens said, helping the company maintain partnerships and coordinate its strategy with major customers.
Related:
Nvidia, AMD Commit $4B to Meta AI Buildout
Dickens argued that Nvidia’s board should evaluate Huang’s continued leadership based on his contributions and the company’s long-term interests, provided investigations find no legal wrongdoing or national security implications.
The company’s ability to retain Huang could be important to preserving the commercial relationships that underpin its position in the AI infrastructure market, Dickens added.
Jeffrey Sonnenfeld, senior associate dean for leadership studies at Yale School of Management, raised a different concern: whether Nvidia’s board has adequately prepared for the possibility that Huang might no longer be able to lead the company.
“There’s been a failure to develop just a succession plan for a crisis, let alone for the future,” Sonnenfeld said, questioning whether the board or Nvidia’s management ranks have the depth to manage an emergency transition.
AI Investment Extends Beyond One Executive
The broader AI infrastructure investment cycle, however, isn’t dependent on Huang alone.
“AI is just too useful in every stratum of the economy to be stopped or even significantly delayed,” said Stephen Sopko, practice lead for semiconductors and deep tech at HyperFrame Research.
Nvidia has demonstrated a forward-looking approach to infrastructure development, investing in technologies such as photonics and software that could otherwise constrain AI deployment, Sopko said. Given that approach, he would be surprised if succession planning weren’t part of the company’s strategy.
Sopko also pointed to the difference between Huang’s personal conduct and the national security questions raised by the investigation.
“The personal failing, while objectionable, is often survivable in global business,” he said. “But the intelligence operative angle, if substantiated, is an entirely different dimension given Nvidia’s criticality to the current US lead over China in AI.”
A prolonged leadership crisis could introduce uncertainty into investments across the semiconductor supply chain. Nvidia relies on Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing for leading-edge processors, while memory suppliers, including Micron, Samsung, and SK Hynix, provide components essential to its accelerated computing systems. Networking and optical-component vendors also benefit from Nvidia’s expanding data center platform.
A leadership change could prompt customers to examine their exposure to a single technology supplier more closely. AMD, Broadcom, and other competitors are already pursuing opportunities in AI accelerators, custom silicon, and networking.
However, Nvidia’s competitive position rests on more than Huang’s public profile. Its CUDA software ecosystem, developer base, engineering capabilities, and integrated hardware platform would remain in place under a new CEO. Competitors would still face the challenge of convincing customers to move workloads away from Nvidia’s established infrastructure.
China Ties Add a National Security Dimension
The investigation comes amid a prolonged dispute over Nvidia’s access to China, one of the world’s largest potential markets for AI computing.
US export controls have restricted China’s access to Nvidia’s most advanced AI processors since 2022. Huang has repeatedly argued that excluding American chipmakers from the market risks strengthening Chinese competitors and weakening US influence over the global AI ecosystem.
Nvidia’s May 2025 earnings call
, Huang described China as a $50 billion AI market that was effectively closed to US industry following restrictions on the company’s H20 processors.
“The question is not whether China will have AI. It already does,” Huang said. “The question is whether one of the world’s largest AI markets will run on American platforms.”
Huang argued that restricting US chipmakers would give Chinese competitors, including Huawei, more room to develop their own technology and compete internationally. He has maintained that allowing American companies to sell into China would help establish US technology as the global standard for AI computing.
In a May 2026
interview
with Channel NewsAsia, Huang also cautioned against the development of separate technology ecosystems.
“It would not be wise to have two distinct artificial intelligence ecosystems created by the US and China,” he said, arguing that the countries could cooperate in AI while competing economically and technologically.
Those arguments reflect both a commercial interest and a broader technology strategy. Nvidia wants access to Chinese customers, while Washington has sought to restrict the transfer of advanced computing capabilities that could strengthen China’s military and technology sectors.
The new Megaspeed investigation adds another layer to those tensions.
Huang defended Nvidia’s business dealings with the Singapore-based company in an October 29 Bloomberg interview, describing the relationship as “normal and not unusual.” He said Nvidia had examined Megaspeed’s GPU deployments to ensure its processors had not been illegally diverted to China.
“We’ve studied all their deployments of our GPUs and counted every one,” Huang said.
The New York Times and The Wall Street Journal have reported allegations of suspected Chinese intelligence activity involving a former Megaspeed executive identified as Alice Huang. Those allegations haven’t been independently established.
Singapore’s Ministry of Home Affairs specifically disputed reporting that its government had investigated Alice Huang or expressed concerns about her relationship with Jensen Huang. The ministry said investigations into Megaspeed were ongoing, and that Singapore expected companies operating there to take foreign export-control requirements into account in their international business activities.
Nvidia’s board said it had no reason to believe company secrets or US national security information were compromised.
Nvidia’s Succession Question
The investigation also puts a spotlight on Nvidia’s leadership structure and whether the company could maintain its strategic direction without its longtime CEO.
Huang has led Nvidia since its founding in 1993, building relationships with customers, suppliers and technology partners over more than three decades. The company hasn’t publicly identified a designated successor.
Even if Nvidia’s engineering and executive organizations can continue operating without Huang, his influence over product strategy and customer relationships presents a different succession challenge.
For the broader AI infrastructure industry, a change in leadership would not necessarily derail investment in computing capacity. Demand for AI systems extends across cloud providers, enterprises and industries, while Nvidia’s technology ecosystem would remain in place.
But the investigation could prompt customers, investors and policymakers to examine how much of Nvidia’s strategic direction depends on one executive – and whether the company has a succession plan capable of preserving its position at the center of the AI infrastructure market.

originally published on TechTarget.com.

title: ContourGlobal plans 300 MW/1.2 GWh battery project in Austria - Energy Storage
content: ContourGlobal is planning a 300 MW/1.2 GWh BESS in Molln, in the Kirchdorf district of Upper Austria. The project would be the largest of its kind in Austria if completed as planned. The company intends to develop the project on land owned by construction company Bernegger. ContourGlobal’s European management chief, Bernhard Haider, confirmed the project location and capacity to pv magazine, but said further details were not yet available. The project remains at an early stage. Media reports say Bernegger secured grid access for the site several years ago, but that authorization was due to expire in mid-2026. A company called ContourGlobal BESS Molln GmbH is expected to obtain the necessary permits in the coming weeks and proceed with project implementation. Bernegger told media outlets that commissioning is expected in 2029. ContourGlobal says it operates power generation assets with a combined capacity of 5.7 GW, including 900 MW of solar and 300 MW of wind power. Its portfolio also includes 16 large-scale battery storage systems with a combined capacity of 600 MW, as well as four further projects totaling 1.1 GW under construction. The company also operates gas-fired power plants. In Europe, ContourGlobal reports nearly 2 GW of operational generation capacity, with 643 MW under construction and a further 894 MW in development. title: Huaneng commissions dual-flywheel frequency regulation system, claims China single-unit power record - Energy Storage
content: China Huaneng Group connected a dual-flywheel frequency regulation system to the grid at its Lanzhou combined heat and power plant on Nov. 6, completing a roughly year-long commissioning process that the group says validates large-scale flywheel storage for coal-fired generation assets. The system comprises two flywheel units with a combined rating of 5.5 MW and 1.375 MWh. The primary unit — a 5 MW, 1.25 MWh flywheel spinning at up to 3,200 rpm on five-axis active magnetic levitation — is claimed by Huaneng to be the highest-power single flywheel unit in China. A secondary 0.5 MW, 125 kWh inertia flywheel handles smaller frequency deviations alongside it. Huaneng says the paired design achieves a grid response time below 100 milliseconds and a regulation accuracy above 99.5%, figures the company attributes to the system’s proprietary control integration with the plant’s distributed control system. These performance figures have not been independently verified. The pairing matters because flywheel storage is not designed for bulk energy delivery — 1.375 MWh is a small buffer — but for speed. Where a lithium battery frequency regulation system typically responds in a few hundred milliseconds, the flywheel array’s sub-100-millisecond response allows the thermal unit to react to grid disturbances faster than its own mechanical inertia would normally permit. The 5 MW primary flywheel handles large frequency excursions, while the smaller unit manages the finer, continuous corrections that would otherwise wear down the larger machine. Technical development was led by the Xi’an Thermal Power Research Institute, Huaneng’s internal R&D arm, which has accumulated experience across several earlier thermal-storage combined frequency regulation demonstration projects. Equipment installation and the mandatory 168-hour continuous trial run were completed in December 2025; the system then operated under monitored conditions before the formal commercial grid connection this month. The Lanzhou plant sits within Gansu province, a core zone of northwest China’s wind and solar buildout. Northwest China’s grids have faced persistent frequency stability challenges as variable renewable capacity has grown faster than conventional dispatchable generation. Thermal plants like the Lanzhou facility are under increasing pressure to act as regulating rather than baseload assets, and grid operators assess financial penalties under China’s two-part ancillary services assessment rules when frequency response falls short of benchmarks. Huaneng’s stated rationale for the flywheel investment is partly to reduce those penalty costs while earning ancillary services revenue. Flywheel storage carries structural advantages for this role — no chemical degradation, a claimed cycle life of tens of millions of charge-discharge cycles, and no fire risk — but remains more capital-intensive per megawatt than lithium battery alternatives at current prices. Whether the dual-flywheel architecture proves economically replicable across other thermal plants will depend on how the ancillary services market values the importance of millisecond-range response. title: Shared grid connection could cut payback for Dutch apartment battery - Energy Storage
content: A 70 kWh battery in a 58-apartment building in the Dutch city of Utrecht would pay for itself in about 0.55 years if the apartments’ individual grid connections were folded into the building’s existing facilities connection, according to a new study from Utrecht University. The researchers said the scenario is notional: they did not assess whether such consolidation is contractually or legally possible. The 1970s 10-story building was renovated to an energy-positive standard in 2019 and 2020, with 356.6 kWp of roof- and facade-integrated PV, roof-mounted heat pumps, and two iwell PowerCube batteries with a combined 70 kWh and 60 kW of discharge power. About 175 kWp of the PV serves the building’s shared facilities, and 181.6 kWp sits behind individual apartment meters. In 2022 the building consumed 200 MWh and generated 255 MWh. The researchers modeled battery dispatch on a full year of measured hourly data from 2022, including a cost for battery degradation. Combining all 58 apartments behind the facilities’ 110.4 kW connection would push summed PV exports past that limit for 122 hours a year, mostly at summer middays. The researchers found the installed battery clears all of those hours, which would let the building drop 58 apartment connections at €350.45 ($393.90) each a year under grid operator Stedin’s tariffs, saving €20,326 annually. In that scenario, after capital and degradation costs, the 70 kWh battery yields a net benefit of €25,297 a year. The economic optimum lies near 280 kWh, at €32,829 a year and a payback of 1.7 years. Varying battery replacement cost by 50% in either direction moves the optimum between 245 kWh and 350 kWh, and payback at 70 kWh stays under one year. Peak shaving adds nothing at this site. Optimized dispatch cuts peak grid import to about 56 kW at the installed capacity, but Stedin’s connection tariff is set in capacity brackets, so the reduction earns no savings. The researchers said per-kilowatt capacity pricing would change that. In the building’s current setup, where the batteries serve only the facilities, there is no peak to shave, and the batteries raise facilities’ PV self-consumption from 37.4% to 53.4%. That is worth a net €4,227 a year, a payback of about 3.3 years, with an optimum near 175 kWh. The measured data also allowed a comparison with the batteries’ installed control system, which was configured for PV peak shaving. Over 7,895 hours of valid metering, facility self-consumption under the default control was 37.5%, against 37.7% simulated with no battery. Optimized dispatch of the same 70 kWh reached 52.8%. The researchers said the default control had little to act on because facility flows never approached the connection limit, and that their optimization assumes perfect foresight, so it marks an upper bound for a real-time controller. The valuation credits no revenue for exported PV, which the researchers said matches the situation once the Netherlands ends net metering on Jan. 1, 2027. The connection saving is not affected by that reform. The study uses hourly data, which the researchers said makes self-consumption figures slightly optimistic, and a single year, 2022, that was above average for solar irradiation in the Netherlands. It combines 2024 Stedin tariffs with 2022 operating data and a 2022 average household electricity price of €0.40/kWh. The work was supported by the TKI Urban Energy Apt-Bat project and the EU Horizon 2020 ARV project. The building, owned by housing corporation Bo-Ex, was the subject of the earlier Apt-Bat project, which included iwell as a partner. That project’s final report found the building could run on a single 3x80A connection with more battery capacity. It said a June 2024 amendment to the Dutch Energy Act made energy sharing possible, but that apartment buildings still face two barriers: residents must remain free to choose their own supplier, and the tax treatment of energy sharing is unclear. The Dutch storage market is expanding ahead of the net metering phase-out, with about 5 GWh of new storage forecast across market segments by the end of 2026 , according to Dutch New Energy Research. The Dutch regulator, the Netherlands Authority for Consumers and Markets, has advised households to self-consume solar power , since suppliers’ feed-in charges will cut returns once net metering ends. Connection capacity is also constrained at the transmission level, where grid operator TenneT has signed a capacity control contract for a 200 MW/800 MWh battery to relieve congestion. The Dutch researchers described their findings in “ Unlocking flexibility in buildings through batteries: a case study of the Netherlands ,” which was recently published in Applied Energy . The post Shared grid connection could cut payback for Dutch apartment battery appeared first on Energy Storage .

title: Vattenfall brings in Kraken to manage entire German battery and renewables fleet as one - Energy Storage
content: The Kraken platform will take turn the standalone and co-located battery storage, wind, and solar assets in Germany into a unified virtual power plant. Swedish utility Vattenfall has selected Kraken to provide control, and management for its grid-scale battery energy storage system (BESS) and renewable generation portfolio in all of Germany. The partnership establishes a control layer connecting Vattenfall’s trading desk directly to its physical assets. The software will aggregate standalone batteries, wind, solar, and co-located sites into a virtual power plant (VPP), automating real-time dispatch across wholesale electricity markets and ancillary services while minimizing imbalance exposure. Germany approved rules for bi-directional charging for storage , allowing co-located batteries to trade grid and solar power (“grey electricity”) without forfeiting EEG subsidies. With this change, utilities now face a dispatch optimization headaches when considering a single grid connection point. Vattenfall’s addition of Kraken’s software capabilities to navigate this regulatory and physical bottleneck aims to avoid cannibalizing its own solar or wind revenues. Sharing grid infrastructure speeds up deployment and reduces connection costs, but can introduce these practical issues. The agreement supports Vattenfall’s broader push into European flexibility markets. Having entered the large-scale battery storage segment in late 2024 with plans to deploy and contract up to 3 GW of battery capacity , the utility has explored and expanded its third-party offtake and optimization business, including signing an industry-first virtual battery tolling agreement with Terralayr . Software control, not trading Vattenfall retains the commercial trading desk and market risk, while Kraken, owned by Octopus Energy Group, acts as the execution engine between the trading algorithm and the inverters. Vattenfall’s approach in taking off-the-shelf dispatch architecture keeps software and hardware integration as a third-party task, reducing operational headaches. The deal comes as Germany’s battery storage additions surged 91% in the first nine months of 2026 to reach 8.2 GWh, increasing competition and reducing the ‘early and easy’ battery revenues available in markets. What they said: Christian Sdralek, director of portfolio management in Vattenfall’s trading unit : “The market for battery storage and co-located renewable assets is growing rapidly. We see significant opportunities to help asset owners maximize the value of their flexibility while supporting the integration of renewables into the energy system. Through our partnership with Kraken, we are strengthening our ability to offer innovative offtake and optimization solutions at scale across Germany and Europe.” Charlotte Johnson, general manager, flexibility at Kraken : “Utilities across Europe are investing heavily in battery storage and renewable generation, but scaling these portfolios requires more than adding new assets. It requires a technology foundation capable of connecting and coordinating different assets as one portfolio. Kraken will give Vattenfall a common platform from its trading desk to its physical assets. Our experience in grid-scale batteries and co-located sites means Kraken can manage the complexity beneath the surface, allowing Vattenfall to focus on growing its portfolio and capturing its full potential.” The post Vattenfall brings in Kraken to manage entire German battery and renewables fleet as one appeared first on Energy Storage .

title: CAT puts century-old train tech to work in its biggest underground machine yet
content:
Electric Heavy Machinery
Caterpillar
Jo Borrás
| Nov 10 2026 - 4:10 am PT
Diesel-electric locomotives have been barreling along America’s wide-open spaces for generations, and the century-old combination of highly efficient diesel engines spinning up generators to power high-torque electric motors has proven tough to beat. Now, Caterpillar is putting that century-old concept to work underground. Meet the CAT R3200 XE LHD.
One of the many hard-working machines moving chunks of Earth under your feet, an LHD (load, haul, and dump) machine is essentially a massive underground wheel loader designed to scoop up blasted rock, haul it through narrow mine tunnels,
then dump it into trucks or ore passes
. Built low and wide to fit in the tunnels, LHDs are workhorses of underground mining operations – and the new R3200 XE is CAT’s biggest yet, with a 25 ton payload and electric drive.
Before we get into the machine’s specs (the few that we have, anyway), I want to make sure understand that large-scale mining operations use obscene amounts of fuel, and a swing in site efficiency of just 1-2%
can mean a huge difference in the bottom line
– and fuel prices were up 27.4% (!)
in August alone
Keep the staggering weight of what that kind of fuel cost can mean to a fleet that buys fuel by the literal truckload as you read the rest of this.
Tier V CAT diesel
Via Caterpillar.
Though not yet officially released by CAT,
snippets of the company’s launch video have been leaking through dealers and trade journals
, and they show the big machine powered by CAT’s newest 18.1 liter Tier 5 C18 diesel generator making 527 hp (~390 kW). That C18 reportedly sends electrons to the same electric drive system used in the company’s already successful 18-ton R2900 XE LHD.
In addition to a bigger generator and heftier payload, CAT says the upcoming R3200 XE LHD offers reduced cycle times versus the R2900 XE with 11% better speed on grade, plus reduced maintenance and repair costs thanks to design refinements for better durability, including redesigned axle. All told, that works out to 28% more tons per hour with 8% better fuel efficiency.
That efficiency is boosted by the same baked-in ADAS tech that’s made the smaller R2900 XE a favorite, and includes the latest version of CAT AutoDig and MineStar, ensuring that the machines are easy for experienced CAT operators to set up for remote, semi-autonomous,
and even fully autonomous operation using Command for Underground
We’ll post an update once CAT makes the full rundown of official specs public, which should be sooner rather than later. When that happens, we’ll see exactly how this big burrowing CAT stacks up against the competition from
. In the meantime, let us know what you think of CAT’s newest electric drive machine in the comments.

title: Genesis launches the flagship GV90 electric SUV in Korea, starting at over $100,000
content:
Peter Johnson
| Nov 10 2026 - 7:07 am PT
opened orders for the ultra-luxury electric SUV in South Korea, with prices starting at over $100,000.
Genesis GV90 prices and driving range in Korea
Hyundai’s luxury brand is moving upscale with the GV90, its first fully electric three-row flagship SUV.
After unveiling the GV90 at the Palace of Fine Arts in San Francisco in August (
which we had the pleasure to see firsthand
), Genesis launched the new “ultra-luxe” SUV in its home market of Korea on Tuesday.
The Genesis GV90 introduces several “world-first” innovations, including the first independently opening and closing B-pillarless coach doors, a 12-airbag roof airbag system, and genuine wood floors with radiant heating.
It’s available in two models: the GV90 Standard with traditional swing doors and the GV90 Neolun, which features the “Neolun Arch Gate,” Genesis’ hidden B-pillar coach door system.
In Korea, the Genesis GV90 Standard 7-seater model starts at 139.5 million won, or about $104,000.
Genesis GV90 Neolun (Source: Peter Johnson/ Electrek)
The GV90 Individual Lounge Seat (6-seater) starts at 145.5 million won ($108,500); the GV90 Neolun Standard (6-seater) starts at 189.9 million won ($141,500), while the top-spec GV90 Neolun Executive Suite (4-seater) starts at 239.5 million won ($178,500).
Based on Hyundai’s new eMP platform, developed exclusively for its flagships, Genesis said the GV90 is like a “moving private lounge,” complete with a multi-chamber air suspension and a dual electronic limited-slip differential (E-LSD).
Genesis GV90 Neolun (Source: Peter Johnson/ Electrek)
A luxury private lounge on wheels
The platform is designed to open up interior space for the B-pillarless coach doors, swivel seats, and more.
When parked, the front seats swivel a full 180 degrees to face rear passengers or to create what Genesis calls “a face-to-face lounge-like configuration.”
The interior is about as over-the-top as you could expect, with massive digital screens, premium materials, and plenty of luxury extras.
The GV90 is the first Hyundai Motor Group vehicle to feature its new extendable display and the first Genesis model equipped with its next-gen Pleos Connect infotainment system.
Together, they create what Genesis calls a new realm of “display expandability.” While other vehicles, like the new Tucson and IONIQ 3, also use Pleos Connect, Hyundai developed an exclusive version for the GV90.
Genesis GV90 Neolun infotainment display (Source: Peter Johnson/ Electrek)
When the vehicle is parked, the screen can expand to 24.6″ at the push of a button, transforming it into a massive Cinematic Display.
Once extended, the display switches to Media Home mode, where you can watch Netflix, live TV, stream music, and more with third-party apps.
A mobile private theater wouldn’t be complete without a premium audio system, right? To top it off, Genesis added a 25-speaker Bang & Olufsen Premier 3D Sound System with Dolby Atmos, so it sounds like you’re actually at the movies.
In place of a traditional instrument cluster, the GV90 has a 25″ Head-Up Display (HUD) that shows the vehicle’s speed, navigation directions, and other ADAS functions directly on the windshield.
The GV90 is also the first Hyundai Motor Group vehicle with a buttonless power system. When you enter the vehicle and close the door, the Motion Column Shifter moves from the 12 o’clock position to the 2 o’clock position.
Meanwhile, the Crystal Sphere between the driver and passenger rotates to indicate it’s ready to drive. The vehicle starts when you press the brake.
Genesis GV90 debut (Source: Peter Johnson/ Electrek)
Dimensions, battery size, other specs
As a full-size flagship SUV, the Genesis GV90 is massive. It measures 208.1″ (5,285 mm) long, 79.9″ (2,030 mm) wide, and 71.5″ (1,815 mm) tall (71.4″ with 24″ tires), with a 127.8″ (3,245 mm) wheelbase.
That’s even bigger than the Hyundai IONIQ 9 (199.2″/5,060 mm in length) and Kia EV9 (197.4″/5,010 mm).
To power a full-size flagship SUV, it needs a big battery. The GV90 uses a 123.5 kWh battery, the largest among Hyundai Motor’s EVs, which Genesis said provides a driving range of 500 km (310 miles) for the 7-seater version with 22″ wheels.
The GV90 Neonlun 6-seater with 24″ wheels has a range of up to 460 km (286 miles) on a single charge.
It’s equipped with a new dual-motor all-wheel-drive (AWD) system that delivers a combined 657 hp (490 kW) and 590 lb-ft (800 Nm) of torque, making it Hyundai Motor Group’s most powerful electric vehicle.
When using a 350 kW fast charger, the vehicle’s battery can recharge from 10% to 80% in about 22 minutes.
Genesis GV90 Neolun (left) GV90 Neolun First Edition (middle) and GV90 (right) Source: Hyundai
“Thanks to the enthusiastic interest and support for the GV90 since its global premiere, we have begun full-scale sales in Korea first,” a Genesis official said, adding the flagship SUV will “set a new standard for luxury.”
Following Korea, Genesis is expected to launch the GV90 in the US and other global markets in early 2027.
Genesis has yet to reveal US prices, but the GV90 Standard model is expected to start at around $100,000. The GV90 Neolun, on the other hand, will likely start closer to $150,000 or more.
What do you think of the flagship Genesis GV90? Would you buy the standard version for about $100,000 or pay the extra for the Neolun with coach doors? Let us know in the comments.

title: Honda shows off its next electric motorcycle, and it’s wilder than you thought
content:
Micah Toll
| Nov 10 2026 - 1:07 am PT
Honda has been getting increasingly serious about electric motorcycles, but if you want to see just how weird the company thinks the future could get, take a look at the Honda EV Outlier Concept.
I got a chance to see the wild-looking machine in person at EICMA in Milan, where it looked like almost nothing else on the show floor. And that’s exactly the point.
The EV Outlier Concept originally debuted at last year’s Japan Mobility Show as Honda’s attempt to imagine an electric motorcycle that isn’t simply a conventional motorcycle with the engine swapped for a battery and motor. In fact, Honda
describes
the concept as looking toward the future of electric motorcycles beyond 2030.
The result is certainly unconventional.
This ain’t your
grandpa’s SuperCub
Instead of a centrally mounted motor driving the rear wheel, the EV Outlier uses motors inside both wheels, giving it all-wheel drive and allowing Honda’s designers to completely rethink the rest of the motorcycle’s layout. The battery is housed in that large central black body, while the rider sits extremely low and behind it.
Honda describes the design philosophy with three words: “Gliding, Ecstasy, and Low.” The first refers to the smooth, nearly silent feeling of electric propulsion, while the second describes the instant acceleration and massive torque available from independently controlled front and rear motors. “Low” is more literal: Honda deliberately dropped the rider’s seating and eye position to create an entirely different sensation from a conventional motorcycle.
There’s even a bucket-style backrest designed to support the rider under hard acceleration and let the rider pivot through corners around their hips.
Up front, traditional mirrors are replaced by cameras, while a wide digital cockpit can display things like lean angle, riding modes, front motor torque adjustment, and what the two wheels are doing in real time.
Will Honda actually build this thing? Almost certainly not exactly as you see it here. That’s what concepts are for.
But the EV Outlier is still interesting as a statement of intent. Honda is obviously still playing around with the freedom that electric drivetrains offer, and the company is asking what motorcycles could become once designers no longer have to work around engines, fuel tanks, transmissions, and traditional drivetrains.
And judging by what I saw at EICMA, Honda’s answer could get pretty wild.

title: Lucid says service wait times fell 20% after 40% jump in service staff
content:
Lucid Motors
Lucid Air
Lucid Gravity
Fred Lambert
| Nov 10 2026 - 6:24 am PT
Lucid (LCID) says service wait times dropped 20% globally in the third quarter after it grew its technician and service-support staff by more than 40% in a single quarter.
The automaker is also adding Studio and Service Centers in Southern California, Los Angeles, Dallas, and the Chicago suburbs, plus 20 more Gravity Mobile Service vans. It’s a clear sign that service had become a problem for Lucid owners.
Lucid hires up service after a year of cuts
Lucid announced the numbers today, a day after its
Q3 2026 earnings
. Both comparisons are against the second quarter, not a year ago.
Lucid’s new combined Studio and Service Center in Mission Viejo, California (Image: Lucid)
The hiring isn’t done either. After a 40%-plus increase in technicians, advisors, and concierges in Q3, Lucid wants that figure at 50% by the end of 2026 and 60% by Q1 2027. Mobile Service capacity in North America grew 15%, with a 40% target for year-end.
That’s a big hiring push for a company that
laid off 18% of its workforce in June
, its second cut in four months after a 12% reduction in February. Roughly 1,500 people left across those two rounds.
And owners noticed. On the LucidOwners forum, one Air Touring owner posted in early October that Lucid told them in writing to expect “a service time of about 7 weeks” at its Beverly Hills Service Center. Other threads blamed service-department layoffs for slow repairs and recall work.
A Lucid technician at work in a Service Center (Image: Lucid)
Billy Hayes, Lucid’s Chief Customer Officer, said the company is “adding service personnel, and increasing Mobile Service capacity to reduce wait times and provide more convenient, responsive support.”
The new Lucid service locations
Here’s what’s opening, according to Lucid:
Mission Viejo, California:
a new combined Studio and Service Center, open now
Downtown Los Angeles and Dallas:
Studio and Service Center operations later this year
Highland Park, Illinois:
Mobile Service:
20 additional Gravity Mobile Service vehicles in North America
Service bays at Lucid’s Mission Viejo location (Image: Lucid)
Lucid is also letting a growing number of its Certified Collision shops handle recall campaign work, which should take some pressure off its own Service Centers.
Outside the US, the expansion leans on partners. Munsterhuis Autobedrijven is Lucid’s first retail partner in the Netherlands (Hengelo), Cloppenburg Automobil SE opens a Duisburg retail and service site in January 2027, Autohaus Possögel starts authorized service in Naumburg, Germany, in December, and Emil Frey France will support Lucid’s launch in France. In Saudi Arabia, Lucid opened its first company-owned Body & Paint Repair Center in Riyadh, with more service sites in Riyadh and Dammam coming in the first half of 2027.
A Lucid Gravity converted for Mobile Service (Image: Lucid)
The numbers Lucid doesn’t give
Lucid doesn’t say what the average wait time actually is.
A 20% drop from seven weeks is still more than five weeks. A 20% drop from one week is a non-issue. Without a baseline, owners can’t tell which one they’re getting.
It’s also hard to separate better service from fewer cars coming in. Lucid
delivered 3,806 vehicles in Q3
, down 7% year-over-year, while it worked through inventory. Its fleet keeps growing, but slowly.
For context, Rivian delivered 19,248 vehicles in Q3, five times Lucid’s volume, and it’s been leaning hard on mobile service too. Lucid is a much smaller operation trying to cover the US, Europe, and the Middle East with a thin network.
Electrek’s Take
This is the right move, and it’s overdue.
Lucid has been one of the few EV startups with genuinely class-leading hardware. The Air’s efficiency is still unmatched and the Gravity is a great vehicle on paper, even if
we found its software wasn’t ready
. But when you’re asking someone to spend $80,000 or more on a car from a brand with an uncertain future, the ownership experience is half the sale. A seven-week wait for a repair kills that sale, and the referrals that come after it.
So growing service staff by 40% in a quarter is a big deal. It also tells you how thin those teams had gotten after two rounds of layoffs. Lucid cut too deep in the wrong place, and it’s now hiring to fix it.
The problem is the timing and the money. Lucid burned $1.04 billion in free cash flow in Q3 and only stays funded into late 2027 because the PIF just added another $1.75 billion. Meanwhile, the Midsize “Cosmos” that’s supposed to bring real volume doesn’t start production until the second half of 2027. Service is exactly where Lucid should spend between now and then, because the buyers it has today are the ones who’ll decide whether anybody trusts the brand with a cheaper EV.

title: Polestar unveils Formula 2030 concept, previewing the next Polestar 2
content:
Polestar
Polestar 2
Polestar 7
Fred Lambert
| Nov 10 2026 - 6:10 am PT
Polestar has now fully unveiled the Formula 2030 concept, a low four-door electric sports car that previews the design of the next-generation Polestar 2 coming in 2027 and the Polestar 7 compact SUV.
The concept sits just 1,350 mm (53 inches) tall, which is lower than the Polestar 5 grand tourer, and it brings physical buttons back into the Swedish brand’s interior.
We reported in September that
Polestar confirmed the Formula 2030 concept
after showing it privately to investors and retailers in Gothenburg. Now we get the full set of pictures and the details.
It’s the first show car built under head of design Philipp Römers, who joined from Audi in 2024.
A low four-door “sports car”
Polestar calls the Formula 2030 a “compact practical four-door sports car” that “sits within its own segment.” It’s 4,680 mm (184.3 inches) long and 2,021 mm (79.6 inches) wide, on a 2,780 mm (109.4-inch) wheelbase.
For context, that’s about 3 inches longer than today’s Polestar 2 and roughly 5 inches lower. It’s also a bit shorter than a Tesla Model 3 and sits 3.5 inches closer to the ground. Polestar says the concept lands “somewhere between” the upcoming Polestar 2 and Polestar 7 in size.
The proportions are classic sports car: long hood, short overhangs, the cabin pushed back over big rear haunches, and 22-inch center-lock wheels. There are gold Brembo calipers behind those wheels and Öhlins dampers on display in the trunk.
Up front, Polestar kept its “Dual Blade” headlights, now set into an aero wing over a shark nose and a deep splitter. The automaker says this is the face of the next-generation Polestar 2 planned for 2027.
There’s a single vertical windshield wiper, like on a race car, and a LiDAR unit that hides under an aerodynamic shroud and only shows itself when the car is driving autonomously.
The rear is where things change the most. Polestar dropped the full-width light bar, which is on just about every EV these days, for what it calls “Single Blade” rear lights. It says they are being introduced here “ahead of series production.”
Römers described the concept as a “bold evolution” of the brand’s existing design:
“It is a physical embodiment of how we apply Polestar’s core values of design, performance and sustainability to the next production cars.”
The rear doors are hinged at the back and there’s no B-pillar, so the whole side opens up to four individual seats.
Physical buttons are back
The interior is built around the driver. A curved 20-inch display, which Polestar calls the “HyperDIM,” is mounted directly on the steering column, and a 12.2-inch center screen sits in the center tunnel.
But the bigger news is below that screen. Polestar added a panel of eight physical controls for the most-used functions, and owners could swap between types of controls, like rocker switches or rotary knobs, and program what each one does.
Polestar says it is “committing to rebalance the mix of physical and digital.” Juan Pablo Bernal, the company’s head of interior design, put it plainly:
“As a performance brand, we see a renewed focus on the driver, and so we re-balance the digital and physical. We introduce physical buttons and controls.”
That’s a big change for a brand whose recent cars run almost everything through the center touchscreen.
The cabin also physically changes with the drive mode. There are three of them: Performance, Normal, and Autonomous. In Performance, the center screen drops flush into the console and the steering wheel and its display pull closer to the driver. In Autonomous, the wheel and the seat move away from each other.
The four seats use inflatable bolsters that shape themselves to each occupant, and the seat backs are made of a flax-based composite instead of virgin plastic. Google Gemini is built in, like in Polestar’s production cars.
A see-through trunk floor
The cargo area is the strangest part of the car. The rear opens as a clamshell, and the trunk floor is transparent, with custom Polestar bags strapped down underneath it with gold straps.
Up front, the frunk holds two race helmets and a fire extinguisher, framed by a gold strut brace.
Now for what’s missing. Polestar didn’t release a single powertrain spec. No battery size, no range, no power output, and no price. This is a design study, and Polestar isn’t saying it will build it.
What it does say is that “various design attributes” from the concept will show up on the next Polestar 2 in 2027 and the Polestar 7 in 2028. Those are two of the
four new models Polestar plans to launch in three years
, and the 7 is going to be built in Europe.
Europe is where this matters, since Polestar is
shut out of the US under the federal connected-vehicle rule
. The concept made its debut during the media drive of the
Polestar 4 SUV
Electrek’s Take
Polestar always impresses me with its design, and this is no exception with this new head of design.
The proportions are sharp. Long hood, cabin pushed back, big haunches, and a roofline lower than the Polestar 5’s on a car with four doors and four real seats. If the next Polestar 2 keeps even half of this stance, it’s going to be the best-looking car in its segment.
I don’t know about the trunk of this thing. Polestar itself calls the rear “UFO-esque,” and between the wraparound glass, the clamshell and the see-through floor, it’s a lot. But everything else on this car is pretty sharp.
Polestar is putting physical controls back in its cars and saying so in plain words. The way they talk about it makes it sound like you can expect that of upcoming production vehicles.
Now the usual caveat. A concept car doesn’t fix a balance sheet. Polestar lost $842 million in the first half of this year on a negative gross margin. Design has never been Polestar’s problem. Building these cars and selling them at a profit is.

title: Unit1 FARO and NEON review: I just found my new favorite e-bike helmets
content:
Micah Toll
| Nov 10 2026 - 7:46 am PT
I test a lot of electric bikes, which means I also spend a lot of time wearing bicycle helmets. And while most helmets tend to fall into the decidedly unexciting category of “necessary safety equipment,” UNIT 1 has managed to make a couple that I actually get excited about wearing.
I’ve been using both the UNIT 1 FARO and the new NEON, and despite taking fairly different approaches, they’ve both become regular go-to helmets for me.
UNIT 1 FARO: High-tech safety with lights everywhere
The FARO is the more futuristic-looking of the two, and it’s also the one that really leans into the “smart helmet” concept.
The helmet includes MIPS protection to reduce rotational impact during a collision, as well as integrated lighting on both the front and rear, including a large customizable rear lighting area made up of dozens of LEDs.
That large rear LED array is a feature I particularly appreciate since visibility is such a major part of cycling safety.
A helmet obviously can’t
drivers to pay attention, but I’d rather give them as many opportunities as possible to see me. The hidden light area below the obvious LED light bar adds a lot of extra visibility.
You can see just how vivid it is in the GIF below, though in real life it looks even better!
The FARO’s lighting system works with UNIT 1’s handlebar remote, which adds turn signals controlled right from the bars.
The system can also provide automatic brake-light functionality, giving you another way to communicate with traffic around you.
I’ll admit that turn signals on bicycles can sometimes feel a bit gimmicky, especially when they’re so close together that drivers can’t really tell which direction is flashing. But putting them high up on the helmet makes them considerably more visible, and the little wireless handlebar remote makes operating them incredibly easy.
The rechargeable lighting is also convenient. I’ve topped up the helmet from a power bank while out and about, meaning you don’t necessarily need to find a wall outlet if you realize your helmet is running low. The rear LED light bar also turns green and illuminates along the length of the bar to let you know what percentage of charge the battery has reached. The only way it could be clearer would be with a screen, but we’re still talking about a helmet here, not a phone.
There are other smart features packed in too, including crash detection and app-based customization.
The tradeoff is weight. At around 640 grams for a medium, the FARO is noticeably heavier than a conventional bicycle helmet. It doesn’t bother me much once I’m riding, and I’ve found the helmet comfortable, but you definitely know there’s more helmet up there. Each time I pick it up, I’m reminded that it’s not just the basic little foam shell that I’ve been wearing for the last few years.
Then there’s the price.
At around $230
(or $195 during the current Black Friday sale period), this isn’t a cheap helmet. You’re paying for all of that technology, lighting, and design.
UNIT 1 NEON: Lighter and perhaps even more practical
As much as I like the FARO, I’ve also become a big fan of the UNIT 1 NEON.
At roughly 430 grams in a medium, it’s significantly lighter than the FARO, and that difference is immediately noticeable. It’s also a bit cheaper at
around $210
(or $178 during the Black Friday sale period) while still packing several of the smart features that make UNIT 1’s helmets interesting.
You still get MIPS rotational protection, crash detection, integrated rear lighting, app connectivity, and compatibility with UNIT 1’s handlebar remote for turn signals and brake-light functionality.
I do wish the NEON had a front light like the FARO. That’s probably the biggest feature I miss when switching between the two. But the NEON makes up for it with one of my favorite features on either helmet: its magnetic face shield.
The shield is ridiculously easy to attach and remove. You don’t even need to carefully line it up. I just need to get it somewhere near the mounting points with one hand and the powerful magnets basically grab it out of the air and snap it into position.
That means I can easily add or remove it one-handed, even while riding.
The photochromic shield is clear enough for night riding but darkens when exposed to bright sunlight, giving you sun protection without requiring separate daytime and nighttime shields. I’ve found that incredibly convenient, especially on rides that transition from daylight into evening. I hate that I can’t wear my sunglasses for eye protection at night, and a lens like this solves that issue.
The NEON also gets something particularly important for faster e-bike riders: NTA 8776 certification. That’s the Dutch standard designed specifically around higher-speed e-bike uses at up to 45 km/h (28 mph). For the Class 3 e-bikes that have become increasingly common in the US, that’s a big distinction compared to helmets rated for crashes at slower speeds.
Which UNIT 1 helmet would I choose?
That’s actually difficult, because I regularly use both.
The FARO is the one I’d choose if maximum visibility and technology were my priorities. I love having LEDs both front and rear, the MIPS protection, and the handlebar-controlled turn signals. It’s comfortable, looks great, and has become one of my favorite urban riding helmets.
But the NEON may be the easier helmet to recommend to most e-bike riders.
It’s lighter, a little cheaper, still gives you a rear light and smart safety features, has that excellent magnetic photochromic face shield, and importantly carries NTA 8776 certification for faster e-bike riding.
Neither helmet is inexpensive, and the FARO in particular asks you to accept some extra weight in exchange for all that technology. But I’m used to wearing much heavier motorcycle helmets and ways.
Plus, it’s important to note that these aren’t helmets I tested for a few rides and then tossed onto a shelf. Both have stayed in my regular rotation, and I find myself reaching for them frequently when I head out on an e-bike. The fact that I not only enjoyed them during my testing but actually replaced my old helmets with them should speak for itself.
For someone who rides as much as I do, that’s probably the strongest endorsement I can give them.
Between solid helmets like these and
safe riding clothing
, it’s good to feel protected!

title: 天合/阿特斯/中节能发布交流纪要，披露光储业务进展
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，近期，天合光能、天合光能、阿特斯、中节能太阳能先后发布投资者交流活动记录公告。3家头部企业围绕2027年光储行业需求、组件价格、储能业务、技术路线等市场关切问题进行披露。
天合光能：前三季度储能出货近10GWh
11月4日，天合光能表示，需求层面，公司预计2027年国内外光伏需求均实现增长。业务策略上，天合将依托销售渠道与品牌优势，聚焦高价值市场，规避过度内卷竞争。
组件价格方面，三季度国内组件价格受多晶硅等原材料影响有所下降，海外地区需求依然保持增长，组件价格总体保持上涨。伴随反内卷相关举措推进，叠加2027年1月1日晶硅组件能效标准落地，天合预计明年组件价格有望保持上涨趋势。
能效产能方面，天合表示，目前公司全部组件产能100%可满足三级能效标准，一、二级能效产能占比80%；预计至2026年底，天合TOPCon3.0高效电池组件产能达到30GW以上。
技术路线上，天合去银化技术已完成储备，后续将根据白银价格波动、行业供需、全产业链导入节奏灵活安排去银化产线改造。
储能业务方面，天合2026年前三季度储能出货已经接近10GWh，其中，主要以海外销售为主。天合预计2027年全球储能市场保持高增，后续将向解决方案服务商转型、拓展新应用场景，持续加大技术与产品投入，规避内卷竞争。
阿特斯：前三季度储能出货9GWh
10月30日，阿特斯发布10月投资者关系活动记录表公告。
阿特斯表示，2026年前三季度，行业面临同质化内卷、价格承压、储能竞争加剧、地缘、汇率、白银及碳酸锂价格波动等扰动。公司认为行业无序竞争的边际效应减弱，行业正从规模扩张阶段转向价值竞争阶段。
2026年前三季度，阿特斯营收186.5亿元，归母净亏损9526万元，亏损主要来自光伏板块及美国业务重塑带来的影响。其中，光伏板块坚持量利平衡，管控业务风险。
储能业务方面，阿特斯前三季度出货9GWh，同比增长约55%，覆盖北美、欧洲、澳洲、拉美等海外市场，在原材料与政策波动下，储能盈利保持稳健。
目前，储能布局上，阿特斯美国市场由合资公司承接，上市公司负责美国以外区域。此外，阿特斯表明，公司不参与低价负毛利竞争，优先保障储能毛利率。碳酸锂下行利好制造端，公司采用浮动定价机制，原材料降价红利周期缩短至约两个季度。相对来说，部分欧美市场储能价格较为坚挺。
对于光伏需求的判断，阿特斯表示，2027年全球光伏预计增速落在10%-15%区间，装机基数抬升后，需要储能配套才能支撑进一步增长。公司此前主动收缩发货规模，计划2027年重回出货增长轨道。国内能效标准公司TOPCon平台可通过技改达标，技改将结合订单、发货计划分步实施。
对于2027年目标，阿特斯称，预期是光伏恢复盈利、储能持续盈利增长。2027年海外储能需求稳中有升，国内储能依赖政策拉动，政策稳定性将决定国内市场空间。
中节能太阳能：TOPCon电池项目已量产
11月5日，中节能太阳能发布最新的投资者关系活动记录表公告，就公司2026年三季度整体运营情况进行交流。
中节能太阳能表示，公司制造端正在推进“智造+服务”转型，公司TOPCon电池项目已实现量产，产能利用率100%、良率95%，达到预期目标。钙钛矿/晶硅叠层技术布局中试线，计划2026年底建成投用，后续将推动前沿技术量产转化，并发展对外技术服务业务，推进轻资产转型。
2026年1-10月，公司新增光伏运营容量1311.24MW，新增开工光伏项目650MW，新增光伏备案1074.94MW，新增独立储能备案4320MW/12287MWh。
国补回款方面，中节能太阳能2026年1月至8月累计收到可再生能源补贴24.42亿元，同比增长5.3%，其中国家补贴23.22亿元，同比增长3.11%；年内已有8个项目完成核查并拨付补贴，公司将持续跟进补录与补贴发放进度。

title: 宁德时代、亿纬锂能等7企储能订单合作落地
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，近期，储能行业订单、项目交付及企业合作动态频出。智光电气控股子公司签订1.14亿元储能系统合同，天赐材料与亿纬锂能达成电解液长期供货协议，晶澳储能交付保加利亚工商储项目。
此外，宁德时代、林洋能源、鹏程无限、果下科技等企业相继与产业链上下游及海外合作伙伴达成合作，涉及储能项目开发、系统集成、供应链协同及海外市场拓展等领域。
智光电气签订1.14亿元储能系统合同
11月7日，广州智光电气股份有限公司发布公告称，其控股子公司广州智光储能科技有限公司近日与某公司签订《某县智慧共享独立储能电站项目储能系统设备买卖合同》，合同金额合计1.144亿元。
根据公告，买方将向智光储能采购储能系统成套设备。智光电气表示，该合同涉及公司主营业务，若顺利履行，预计将对公司本年度及未来年度经营业绩产生积极影响。
天赐材料与亿纬锂能签45万吨电解液长协
11月6日，天赐材料发布公告称，公司全资子公司九江天赐高新材料有限公司近日与惠州亿纬锂能股份有限公司签订《长期供货协议》，约定2027年至2029年向亿纬锂能供应预计需求量为45万吨的电解液产品。
根据协议，双方同意按照需求预测数量上下浮动20%执行订单，具体采购数量、单价及质量标准等以双方确认的采购订单、质量协议等文件为准。协议自双方签字盖章之日起生效，有效期至2029年12月31日。
天赐材料表示，本次协议的签订有利于双方建立长期稳定的合作关系。如果协议得到充分履行，预计将对公司2027年至2029年度经营业绩产生积极影响。不过，实际采购量及金额仍以具体订单为准，协议履行存在一定不确定性。
晶澳储能交付保加利亚工商储项目
近日，晶澳储能在保加利亚塞夫利耶沃交付一个工商业储能项目，项目配置6台JAPlanet工商业储能一体机，储能规模为0.75MW/1.566MWh，并与现场已有的250kWp光伏电站协同运行。
据悉，晶澳储能此前已向该客户累计交付多个项目、数十台JAPlanet工商业储能一体机。
鹏程无限与天顺智慧能源签署合作协议
11月6日，深圳鹏程无限新能源有限公司与深圳天顺智慧能源科技有限公司签署战略合作协议，双方将围绕电芯采购、储能系统集成及战略投资等方面开展合作，进一步加强产业链上下游协同。
根据协议，双方将本着发挥各自优势、互利互惠、合作共赢的原则，在电芯采购、储能集成、战略投资等方面开展合作，推动具体事项落地。此外，双方还就战略投资等资本层面的合作可能性进行了探讨。
宁德时代与中铝集团签署战略合作协议
近日，宁德时代与中铝集团在福建宁德签署战略合作协议，双方将围绕有色金属新材料研发、再生金属循环利用、绿电直连与储能、高海拔源网荷储及全球化产业链配套等领域开展合作。
林洋能源与LG新能源签署合作协议
11月5日，林洋能源与LG新能源正式签署战略合作协议，双方将围绕储能电站开发、储能系统集成及智慧运维服务等领域开展合作。
合作将优先推动南通电网侧独立储能项目落地，同步联合推进南京独立储能项目，逐步将合作版图拓展至全省乃至全球同类项目。其中南京项目涵盖电站开发建设、智慧运维及配套能源服务等多项内容。
下一步，林洋能源与LG新能源将成立专项工作专班，建立高层常态化沟通机制，推进相关示范项目落地。
果下科技与Micmar建立战略合作关系
11月3日，果下科技海外储能品牌HANCHU ESS（汉储）宣布，与赞比亚本地合作伙伴Micmar正式建立2027年度战略合作伙伴关系。双方将围绕本地化市场布局、储能产品推广及能源服务等方面深化合作，共同拓展赞比亚储能市场。
根据合作规划，双方将发挥各自在产品与本地市场资源方面的优势，为赞比亚市场提供储能产品及能源服务，进一步推动储能业务落地。作为合作举措之一，双方还将联合打造储能移动展车，作为产品展示与本地化服务载体，向当地市场推广储能产品及解决方案。

title: 总投资8亿，中润光能16GW光伏电池项目技改推进
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，安徽省滁州市生态环境局发布《中润新能源（滁州）有限公司高效大尺寸光伏电池技改项目生态环境影响报告书》受理公示。
根据环评报告，2022年7月，中润光能控股子公司中润新能源（滁州）有限公司在滁州市琅琊经济开发区拓展区投资约105亿元建设年产16GW高效光伏电池项目，该项目分两期实施，每期年产能为8GW，分别先后于2023年8月和2025年2月完成自主竣工环保验收。
此次技改项目主要针对现有光伏电池生产线进行工艺及设备升级，总投资8亿元。具体来看，电池车间1拟将现有16条TOPCon生产线全部改造为TBC型生产线，对整线设备及相关湿法、高温、镀膜、丝网、测试等辅助设备进行技术升级，淘汰部分原有设备，新增LP、光刻、划片、喷墨等设备。
电池车间2对现有16条TOPCon生产线实施升级改造，通过导入背激光技术、边缘钝化技术和银包铜技术等先进工艺，降低长波长光寄生吸收、修复电池切割边缘缺陷，预计可使电池转换效率提升0.2%以上、组件效率获得0.3%以上的综合增益，组件功率达到740W以上、超过二级能效标准，同时减少贵金属银用量，有效降低制造成本、增强产品价格竞争力。
此次技改主要围绕现有光伏电池产线的工艺和设备升级展开。技改完成后，中润新能源将进一步调整现有电池产线的技术结构。

title: 杉杉股份、通合科技等推进4大储能产业链项目建设
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，11月伊始，国内储能电池产业多个项目迎来新进展。
通合科技拟建算力储能一体化项目
11月6日，通合科技发布公告，拟与石家庄高新区科技创业园区管理办公室签署进区协议书，投资建设“算力储能一体化智能成套电源装备产业化项目”，项目总投资为10.025亿元。
该项目拟落地石家庄高新技术产业开发区兴安大街东侧通合电子南侧地块，项目建设内容涵盖数据中心用供配电系统及模块研发生产（二期）、新型储能系统产业化以及智能一体化电源系统产业化等板块。
杉杉股份拟建储能与动力电池材料基地
11月5日，杉杉股份发布公告，公司向特定对象发行A股股票事项已获得间接控股股东海螺集团国资批复。本次定增拟募资不超过40亿元，由海螺集团以现金全额认购，其中25亿元将专项投向内蒙古年产15万吨锂离子电池负极材料一体化基地项目。
该一体化项目总投资约51.06亿元，落地包头市青山区，规划建设周期17个月，计划于2027年3月开工、2028年7月竣工。
面对全球储能与新能源汽车高速发展带来的旺盛负极材料需求与产能缺口，该基地的建设将进一步完善公司一体化产业链配套与产能供给。
8GWh储能电池项目落地衡阳
11月4日，衡阳国投集团旗下弘新公司、领湃研究院与湖南恒泰富鑫正式签约，合作推进祁东高新区归阳园区祁东电芯工厂1号、3号生产线及相关设备建设。
该项目聚焦新型储能与动力电池制造，将推进改造2GWh产线，并新建8GWh电池生产线及钠电池生产线。

弘元绿能600MW组件交付及5.62MW项目并网

title: Can We Trust AI Agents When Zero Trust Isn’t Really Zero
content:
This article is brought to you by Queen’s University Belfast.
Several teams around the globe are leveraging AI by creating a task force of agents managed by an orchestrator and creating applications to support risk assessment, client profiling, match making, and information yield with a slight overview of decision making. One of the important components for these agents is to ensure that the logs are managed and historic relevance is not being used to avoid skewing towards same decision making. Thus, the system is expected to keep checkpoints in place where agents are prompted to delete such historic relevance.
However, despite such methodology in place, a future prompt could make the agents bring forward the information that was supposed to be deleted and can be tricked into revealing more information, which is a classic case of context recovery attack. So, the question raised here is: How can we trust that our instructions have been followed? And where is the proof?
There is an element of utilizing zero-trust architectures (ZTA) for orchestrating and managing agentic activity, which simply means all agentic interactions use the core principle of “never trust,” “always verify.” ZTA components include a policy enforcement point (PEP) that has to be trusted to maintain trust across the system, so the question that remains is where is the component of zero-trust, and shall we trust the policies enforced by PEP?
Having a pro-agentic approach and utilizing agents could be helpful with the right guardrails in place. Opening our systems to random agents that are being trained on off-the-shelf models and blindly relying on them can pose significant cyber risks. For example, vibe coding by using an AI model to help develop software, giving away the entire codebase to an untrusted entity outside the organization can lead to vulnerability sweeping across multiple surfaces.
Vibe coding by using an AI model to help develop software, giving away the entire codebase to an untrusted entity outside the organization can lead to vulnerability sweeping across multiple surfaces.
This opens critical discussions towards how vibe coding could interfere with the positioning and implementation of trusted execution of the agentic queries. Consider an autonomous web of agents that relies on agents’ inputs to drive the operations. When the system is operating under low tolerance of failure and with non-tracking based agentic workflows, it could be computationally expensive to trust and verify each query in real-time that leads to the common trade-offs of memory vs execution.
Another risk to consider is the zero-day attack. When it happens, how will the system react? Would such an event be manageable without a total infrastructure breakdown? The scale of impact can be observed from over reliance on agentic ecosystems with only one trusted layer. This could mean that when failure occurs, the entire ecosystem could be exposed, just like there will be no autonomy if the backbone network is not available, which essentially means no layer to place trust.
How quickly can de-authentication attacks occur?
An in-house experiment done at Queen’s University Belfast (QUB) provided an initial understanding of how the scale of agentic attacks could mean a lower window of vulnerability. The team focused on very popular de-authentication attacks and with agentic orchestration, the swift rate to do de-authentication attacks could go as low as 2 to 3 seconds. This gives little to no time to react and decide on patching the system.
There is another aspect of the large-scale agentic system, which establishes trust under asynchronous autonomy. Trust serves as a critical foundation for traceability. How would you ensure that all the agents operating towards a common goal are aligned and understand the delays associated with their goals?
Our team worked around this space, which at first involved demonstrating that the problem exists, and its impact and scale can be huge when you must prove trust under boundaries of asynchronous autonomy. Solutions towards such problems can be simplified by keeping things like AI-bill of material or leveraging distributed ledger technology that can provide underlying infrastructure of trust via traceability and immutability and keep the agentic activity and associated trust vectors agnostic to the platform.
Within trust, another factor that is not well explored but needs a thorough investigation is the concept of horizontal anomalies. It defines how agents interact differently with various sources under different settings. As agents behave correctly and align themselves with the architectural expectations for one specific task or application, that does not necessarily mean these can be trusted for their operations across all associated components. How to identify such anomalies and what methods can be employed without complying with such agents remain open questions and topics for further exploration.
The critical aspect is that utility of agents with semi to low trust governance offer short-term high benefits, but the cost of recovery when the system fails is yet to be explored, and this will not be a contained issue. We are looking into the system where agents are already sweeping into different entities and may not allow complete recovery. For example, a mere supply chain issue because an agent going rogue is now not a containable small task but needs sweeping across all the touch points of those affected agents. This essentially means despite the number of agents and their ability to trigger proxy-agents, which may not be directly linked to the wider ecosystem, there is a need to ensure that computationally expensive trackers are in place for all the agents.
Other relevant PhD works carried out in our research group are towards sovereignty of AI, exploring aspects of trust and accountability. Our hypothesis is that sovereignty and trust need to be governed together as onus of provenance is high on the host of agents. Thus, it needs understanding of laws governing trust-based executions of AI. The important challenge here is that there is a vital difference between missed information and missed instructions, and both have different impacts when it comes to trusted accountability.
Does true zero-trust architecture exist?
The real-world issue with these systems lies in the failure to adopt approaches that historically have relied on state-based modeling when governing trust. In stateless systems where agentic autonomy is high, the convergence and reliability towards trust-provenance decreases significantly. Thus, it brings us back to the original question – does a true zero-trust even exist?
Can policies be trusted? If so, how should these be managed without falling into the trap of policy-based accessibility and control issues? Despite the argument that PEP can help manage access between the agents, placing a single entity and expecting it to scale towards all agentic interactions is underestimating the problem space.
Formal verification of trust is another part of a trust-based agentic ecosystem. When dealing with AI models, understanding the robustness helps to put trust in place for these models.
To build our case and settle around the challenges of trust embeddings in Agentic AI, within Cyber AI hub, we are exploring opportunities to help companies scale up as well as build their pipeline of agentic applications for commercial viability. However, the element that governs our regular work and decision making are scale of problem and number of agentic deployments, anomaly detection across the agentic workflows, continuous evaluation of the attack surfaces and vulnerability assessment, exploring differences in the pure agentic AI and task-driven multi-agent system.
We are working with industries where trust is a pre-requisite, and these organizations put trust as a guardrail managed via internal policies with a pure focus on securing the systems through policies rather than trusting the third-party agentic service providers. Additionally, trust in services is presented by ensuring constraints around their service models where agentic activities are tracked and managed via logs including management of their token revocation list to avoid replay attacks depending on the type of application. Formal verification of trust is another part of a trust-based agentic ecosystem. When dealing with AI models, understanding the robustness helps to put trust in place for these models. Things like balancing the adversarial accuracy along with certified adversarial robustness can help to determine how much the model can be trusted.
But the question is, can we settle for anything less than foolproof when it comes to deployment of agents in the real world? And if so, how much impact can be controlled, and who is responsible for the remaining component?

title: BMW Is Embracing Cheaper LFP Batteries For Its Newest EVs
content:
BMW's newest EVs boast impressive range. Now cheaper batteries could help bring their prices down, even if it means fewer miles.
Photo by:
Andrei Nedelea
2:14pm ET
BMW will add cheaper LFP batteries to selected EVs, potentially lowering prices.
Its compact Neue Klasse EV, due in 2028, looks like a likely candidate, though unconfirmed.
BMW is expanding battery sourcing in Europe and the U.S., but local production doesn’t guarantee lower costs.
Between the 435-mile
and 468-mile
, BMW’s newest EVs make a strong case for spending a bit more to get incredible range. Now the company is looking at accommodating buyers who don’t need that much range and would rather keep some extra money in their pockets.
Speaking during BMW’s third-quarter earnings call, CEO Milan Nedeljkovic confirmed that the company will expand its use of
lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries
for Neue Klasse EVs, potentially opening the door to more affordable electric BMWs. BMW considers the cylindrical nickel-manganese-cobalt cells that are in most Neue Klasse cars as superior for the range they deliver, he said, but he acknowledged that
LFP offers a different balance of cost and range
“We will add the LFP technology in our vehicles, but we will be very specific in which vehicle and for which purpose,” Nedeljkovic said without naming the next models getting it or specifying a launch date outside China. Nor did he promise that lower battery costs would translate directly into lower sticker prices.
Photo by: Andrei Nedelea
China already offers a preview of the strategy. The entry-level,
long-wheelbase iX3
30L uses a 77-kilowatt-hour LFP battery, while the more expensive 40L and 50L have NMC packs. The 30L has a claimed CLTC range of 630 kilometers (391 miles), although the Chinese test cycle is more optimistic than WLTP and EPA.
LFP's cost advantage starts with what goes into it. The cathode it uses is relatively inexpensive iron and phosphate instead of the nickel and cobalt found in NMC cells. It’s also known to generally offer high longevity, thermal stability, and less degradation from frequent fast charging to 100%. The catch is lower energy density, which makes NMC more attractive, especially for longer-range applications.
could introduce LFP versions of existing models, following the Chinese iX3’s example. Its forthcoming smaller Neue Klasse EV also looks like a strong candidate for LFP. BMW has confirmed a compact Euro-focused electric model is coming in 2028, bringing its new technology into a more affordable segment.
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
Choosing cheaper batteries would make particular sense for an application targeting more budget-conscious buyers.
Mercedes already demonstrates how this can work within one lineup.
The electric CLA
—likely a direct rival to BMW’s upcoming
cheaper Neue Klasse EV
—has a larger 85-kWh battery option with NMC chemistry, plus an entry-level variant that gets a 58-kWh LFP pack. Buyers can choose between a lower entry price and the extra range offered by the bigger battery, without switching to an entirely different car.
Meanwhile, BMW is expanding where its battery cells come from. It announced a deal with Samsung SDI to supply Gen6 cells from Europe and LG Energy Solution from the U.S., starting toward the end of the decade. Samsung joins CATL and EVE Energy in BMW’s European cell supply network, although none of these agreements identify the cells they will supply as LFP.
BMW’s cheaper chemistry could help contain costs, but the badge will still fetch a premium, so it will likely still be more expensive than similar offerings from mainstream brands.

title: Ford's Radical New EV Manufacturing Process Is Already Building Trucks
content:
Ford has built its first Fathom electric pickups on its Louisville production line. Now it needs to prove the process can scale.
Photo by:
1:44pm ET
Ford has already started testing production of the Fathom.
Vehicles are rolling off the line for validation testing, with about 90% of the testing already complete.
Actual customer deliveries aren't slated until late next year.
During its recent quarterly earnings call, one Ford executive revealed that it has already begun rolling Fathoms off the line at its
recently revamped factory in Louisville
well ahead of the affordable electric pickup's
late-2027 delivery schedule
"It's progressing very well," said Ford COO, Kumar Galhotra, during the company's recent quarterly earnings call. "90% of the validation testing has been completed. We've built our first production line vehicles at Louisville assembly plant."
Photo by: Ford
Importantly, Galhotra didn't say these are production vehicles. Rather, these are the first Fathoms built on their real production line. Essentially, these validation vehicles are the beginning of Ford proving out its production process for both the Fathom and its Universal Electric Vehicle Platform. It's an important milestone for Ford, which has bet its electric future on the UEV platform and a radically different method of manufacturing cars than it's used before.
Ford will build the Fathom using a so-called "assembly tree" rather than the assembly line Henry Ford pioneered a century ago. The front, middle, and rear sections of the pickup will be put together simultaneously, then joined together toward the end of the process. Ford says this should allow it to build vehicles quicker and more efficiently, in part by making the ergonomics better for its workers. It resembles the
"unboxed" process
Tesla has introduced for the Cybercab.
Ford has been building cars for more than a century, but a new EV on a new platform using new manufacturing techniques needs to be fleshed out—especially if Ford wants to quickly hit the production volumes it's reportedly targeting:
100,000 sales in the first year
. As Tesla CEO Elon Musk said in the midst of the company's period of production hell: "It's relatively easy to make a prototype, but extremely difficult to mass manufacture a vehicle reliably at scale."
The testing isn't just limited to the Louisville plant where more than $2 billion was invested to manufacture the Fathom. Ford's Shelbyville Technical Center has also been cranking out large castings used to underpin its affordable electric pickup.
These large castings are made in a
similar way to Tesla's Gigacasting process
with the goal being to cut down on the production complexity (and cost) of the Fathom. In total, it takes 146 different parts into just 2 large castings. Galhotra says that Ford has already made 5,000 of these unicastings and has effectively substantiated its ability to build this new tech at a high rate.
The next challenge, according to the COO, is the rest of the supply chain:
"We need to make sure that the supply base can run at rate with high quality parts," said Galhotra "And that's very normal at this stage of the launch, and that's what we're going to be working on for the next few months."
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
The Blue Oval
doesn't plan on delivering any of these pickups for about a year
, which means that it still has time to ramp things up and make sure the so-called "assembly tree" is running smoothly. The
Fathom could prove out to be Ford's EV redemption arc
if the automaker gets it right. Affordable?
. Versatile?
. Scalable? That's to be seen.

title: Honda Is Betting $3 Billion On Hybrids As It Pulls Back From EVs
content:
Honda Is Betting $3 Billion On Hybrids As It Pulls Back From EVs
The automaker had ambitious plans for EVs in the U.S. Now, it’s spending big on a new factory and a new hybrid lineup.
- Honda is spending $3 billion on a big hybrid push in the U.S.
- The company is building a new car factory in Ohio, which will be able to accommodate gas, hybrid, and electric cars.
- Elsewhere, the automaker is retooling factories to get them ready for the upcoming hybrid boom.
Honda is building a new car factory in the United States, which will primarily manufacture hybrid and traditional gas vehicles. The new facility, which is estimated to cost $3 billion, will be Honda’s fourth auto plant in Ohio and the company’s ninth car-related production facility in the U.S.
The move is part of the Japanese automaker’s push to introduce no fewer than 15 new hybrid models globally, with the majority of them being destined for the American market, too. It’s also Honda’s first big step away from its ill-fated electric-car push, which ended up with a completely new vehicle platform and three EVs being retired before even one production-ready unit had rolled off the assembly line.
Honda's New Manufacturing Plant Location In Ohio
As a reminder, the Acura RSX, Honda 0 Series Saloon, and Honda 0 Series SUV were supposed to go into production at a new EV hub in Ohio, but the entire plan was scrapped due to major financial losses. After canceling the 0 Series project, the company posted its first loss in nearly 70 years, with $9 billion going down the drain.
After the whole EV debacle, Honda decided to go back to the drawing board and chose ultra-efficient hybrids as its next big thing in the U.S. The car manufacturer is already knee-deep in the development of multiple hybrid models, with the first cars expected to debut in 2028.
To support the new strategy, Honda’s new plant, which is located right next to three of its other facilities in Ohio, is scheduled to become operational in 2029. According to the company, the new location will add over 2,000 jobs and will be able to manufacture 240,000 vehicles annually, raising the automaker’s total annual U.S. production capacity to 1.3 million cars. What’s more, the new Ohio plant will increase Honda’s hybrid powertrain system capacity by 250% in the state.
Honda's new Ohio auto plant location in relation to current Honda facilities
All this being said, the latest Ohio factory is being built with flexibility in mind. Despite being aimed at hybrids at first, the company said that it will be able to add EVs into the mix in the future, if needed.
Elsewhere, Honda is investing in retooling factories to support its big hybrid push. The Alabama Auto/Engine Plant, the Anna Engine Plant in Ohio, the Transmission Plant in Ohio, and the Transmission Plant in Georgia are undergoing upgrades right now, adding equipment and new lines.
Earlier this year, when the car manufacturer announced its hybrid plans, two new vehicles were brought on stage: a Honda-badged sedan and an Acura-badged crossover. Neither has been confirmed, but we do know that electric all-wheel drive will be offered as part of the next-generation hybrid powertrain, and that crossovers will make up most of the lineup.
According to the Japanese automaker, the new system is designed to deliver 10% more efficiency than the current generation that debuted in 2023.

title: Land Rover Is Going After BYD Over This Alleged Defender Lookalike: Report
content:
Jaguar Land Rover is challenging BYD over its Defender-like SUV. The dispute has already prompted raids on BYD's Dutch offices.
Photo by:
4:37pm ET
BYD's offices in the Netherlands were reportedly raided as part of a legal dispute with Jaguar Land Rover.
Bailiffs collected digital records over allegations that BYD may have reversed-engineered the Land Rover Defender to build the BYD Ti7.
Court proceedings begin later this week, just as the Ti7 hits the showroom floor in Europe.
Court-appointed bailiffs reportedly raided two BYD offices on behalf of Jaguar Land Rover. The issue? JLR reportedly has a problem with the Chinese automaker's Ti7, alleging that it infringes on the UK-based firm's intellectual property.
reports that two BYD offices in the Netherlands were raided back in August over the alleged copycat model. During the raid, bailiffs seized digital records related to the development of the Ti7. According to the report, a Dutch court will decide later this week whether JLR's claims against BYD can proceed. The Ti7 should reach European customers soon.
Photo by: BYD
Both BYD and JLR declined to comment when reached by InsideEVs sister site
Visually, the similarities between the the
Ti7 and Land Rover Defender aren't hard to understand. But there might be more to it than just BYD having a similar boxy styling. According to
The Times
, JLR suspects that engineers at BYD may have dismantled and reverse engineered a Defender as part of the R&D process.
That alone isn't really an uncommon practice. Heck, any automaker worth its salt benchmarks models from competitors. But if BYD used any of that proprietary and protected tech in the production version of the Ti7, it could be a bigger problem.
BYD originally launched the Ti7 in China in September 2025 starting at under $27,000. It released a battery-electric back in April for $29,900 and plans to begin delivering the Ti7 in Europe as early as January.
European versions of the Ti7 start at around $64,500 versus the comparable 7-seater version of the Land Rover Defender 110 running nearly $92,000. Naturally, you can see why JRL might be a bit miffed about BYD coming to market in Europe with the Ti7.

and Chinese brand

. While it lost the case against Ineos, it did win the 2019 legal battle against Jiangling, finding that its Landwind X7 was too similar to the
