title: 千问办公2.0卷向Team Agent，我们用它跑了一遍编辑部日常
content:
千问办公2.0卷向Team Agent，我们用它跑了一遍编辑部日常
办公AI结束单机模式
听雨 发自 凹非寺
量子位 | 公众号QbitAI
量子位后台工作大公开！
每天，咱编辑部几个群里都在聊选题。新闻线索刷屏，谁来跟、什么时候交、进展到哪一步，都得有人把这些事捋清楚。
这次，我们拉来了一位AI同事。
总结群聊记录、派选题、建待办、催ddl，它都能上手：
甚至还能帮忙写初稿……
编辑部的日常工作，千问办公这回全给包圆了啊。
（不是，那还要我干什么）
这次千问办公的2.0版本，是公测三个月以来最大的一次升级。
界面焕新之外，千问办公2.0推出了行业首个支持多人与Agent协作的功能——「协作」，还上线了人机共创、自动任务、资料空间和三端互联等多项能力。
在官方博客中，团队对千问办公2.0的定位是：Team Agent。
简单说，就是让Agent加入团队，和多位成员一起推进工作。
在千问办公2.0里，团队可以建立协作空间，把项目相关的钉钉群聊和资料关联进来，让Agent了解大家正在忙什么。
同事补充了新信息，或调整了任务要求，后续工作就能结合这些背景继续推进。
哎，这个方向是不是有点眼熟？
今年6月，Anthropic在Slack推出了Claude Tag测试版。同一频道里的团队成员可以@同一个Claude，接着彼此的对话推进任务。
千问办公的Team Agent则将Agent与团队已有的办公工具和工作流原生打通，大家日常使用的群聊、文档、会议纪要，也就成了AI参与协作的工作环境。
效果究竟如何？我们实测走起～
项目信息跨群归拢，千问办公接管跟进
千问办公2.0，最主打的核心功能就是协作。
在左侧栏创建一个协作空间，邀请同事加入，再把项目相关的钉钉群聊关联进来，群里的讨论就成了AI了解这项工作的背景。
一个项目分散在多个群里，可以把它们关联到同一个空间；项目相关的AI听记、云文档和本地资料，也能一并加入。
这样一来，小Q处理任务时，就能结合群里的讨论和已有资料，了解事情的来龙去脉。
这里我就把钉钉录音卡里的所有AI听记，以及本地的各种资料文件，统统上传了。
（不得不说钉钉录音卡还是蛮好用的）
还关联了钉钉的三个群聊：量子位选题群、图文群和视频群。
这三个群吧，里面各有负责的同事，大家平时在群里分享新闻线索、报选题，讨论得那叫一个七嘴八舌。
图文和视频关注的新闻又经常重合，同一个选题聊着聊着，就可能串到了另一个群。
想知道最近有哪些题、谁在跟、什么时候交，就免不了来回翻聊天记录。
把这三个群关联到千问办公的协作空间后，就可以直接让千问小Q帮忙整理：
帮我把关联的三个群捋一下，现在有哪些题、谁在跟、哪些卡住了？标一下信息来自哪个群。
小Q随后列出了一张选题进度表，把分散的讨论汇总到一起，还附上了对应的群聊来源：
汇总好选题进度表后，哪些选题要赶时效性，哪些可以慢慢打磨，也可以让小Q根据群聊内容判断。
比如，最近GPT-6.2要发了，但相关选题还得等官方发布消息，有消息再跟进；Thinking Machines的新模型报道已经进入排期，有约定的初稿时间。
同事报的有关Jeff Dean和奥特曼的两条选题，则需要先理清原文，暂时不定交稿时间。
交初稿、审核、正式发布的时间，也可以要求它分开列，尚未确认的就保留待定：
视频群这边，也可以梳理相关群聊内容，汇总选题：
小Q也把这部分内容都整理好了，最后汇总成一个任务看板：
这里我发现，你最好明确@千问小Q，它才会回复。
不然容易像我这样出现如下情况……
无人理睬啊(：з」∠)
或者，你也可以在右侧把回复规则设为自动判断。聊到它熟悉的资料或正在跟进的工作时，小Q会结合上下文，判断要不要接话。
除了我布置任务以外，别的同事也可以直接@小Q，询问自己的任务要求：
而且我还发现一个很心机的玩法，如果你不想在群里直接艾特人布置任务，就可以让小Q代劳……
多好啊，这样就不会惹人烦了，反正都是AI的锅。
小Q还会根据钉钉群聊的内容动态更新任务进展，给出最新判断。比如Thinking Machines这篇稿子，我一直在群里找人认领。
这时候视频群里有同事给出了回复，小Q就根据最新消息更新了任务认领情况：
但如果这活实在没人想干，也可以让小Q先干了，比如写个初稿：
生成的产物也会在右侧显示：
它还可以根据任务进展，自动设置定时任务。
比如Thinking Machines这篇稿子，ddl定了15:00交付，它就自己创建了一个14:00提醒的任务：
啊，看着好有压力啊……
你可能会觉得，我平时也不报选题啊。
换成运营活动、电商上新或产品迭代，类似的协作需求也是存在的：项目进展分散在不同群里，分工和排期随时调整，换个人接手又得重新解释背景。
从上面的实测可以看出，千问办公2.0已经能围绕团队正在推进的工作，串起跨群信息整理、任务认领、待办创建和后续提醒，让分散在群聊里的讨论，逐步落实到工作安排上。
原来的钉钉群继续承担日常交流，协作空间则把获授权的群聊和项目资料汇集起来，供团队共同使用。
这套用法既适合跨周期、跨群的大项目，让信息同步、任务跟踪更及时；也适合编辑部周会这类例行事项，让每周讨论不用从零开始。
群里有了新进展，大家也可以在千问办公里让小Q重新核对信息、调整安排。
这也是Team Agent与Personal Agent在工作组织方式上的区别。
Personal Agent主要围绕个人的任务和偏好展开；Team Agent围绕团队共同推进的项目，让多名成员共享工作背景，向同一个AI补充信息、提出要求。
和以群内问答、消息通知为主的常规群聊机器人相比，协作空间里的小Q，更接近一个持续跟进项目的AI项目经理。
它不仅可以结合多个群聊和资料推进项目，你还可以给它添加技能、设置回复规则，或者定时任务。
技能市场里面的skill，以及专家套件还是蛮丰富的，大家可以自行探索一下：
从中也能看出千问办公2.0的价值：让团队少做几次信息搬运和重复解释，就能把更多精力放在判断方向、解决问题和完成交付上。
在线改稿、主动干活，Agent当起办公搭子
此外，千问办公2.0还上新了人机共创、自动任务、资料空间和三端互联功能。
在千问办公2.0里，对话和文档可以左右并排呈现，你和AI能在同一个窗口里完成讨论和修改。
除了Word、Excel、PPT这套Office老三样，人机共创还支持钉钉文档和AI表格。
先拿PPT试试。上传一份普通的PPT，选中需要调整的几处内容，分别写下修改意见，再一次提交：
提交之后就按要求改好了～
钉钉文档也可以这样改。比如，一份新品推广方案需要局部调整，我可以直接选中对应文字，告诉它怎么改。
先精简服务内容，拆成必选的基础方案和可选增项，说明各自的作用；再调整报价，两部分分开列出；交付安排则按客户要求，改成分阶段确认。
这三项修改，可以分别选中文档里的三处文字，各自输入意见，最后一次提交：
很快，千问办公2.0就按照要求，把修改落实到了原方案文档里：
AI表格也可以用同样的步骤操作，多处输入修改意见，一键提交：
我还发现，千问办公2.0有个邪修功能。
那就是设置自动回复。
比如我告诉千问办公，选题群里有人@我提出补稿或补充资料的要求时，就在群里回复「收到，我看看」，然后再结合相关群聊和已有参考资料，整理一份补稿清单私发给我。
亲测有效。以后再也不用担心领导突然在群里艾特我了。
但底下会有个「千问办公」的角标，大家都知道是AI发的，所以该干的活还是得干……
不过千问办公2.0也通过钉钉把所需资料私发给了我，还是省了不少事
当然，比较实用的场景，还包括客户接待和项目跟进。
如果你是电商运营，就可以设定一个自动操作：用户群里有人反馈差评时，就自动读取订单信息和上下文，生成一条处理建议并发给自己。
如果你是销售，就可以提前设定：客户群里有新人加入时，自动发送欢迎语，并附上产品介绍手册。
如果你是门店区域经理，就可以设定，当补货群里有人@你说缺货时，读取库存表，向仓库负责人发起调货申请。
这些场景，用的都是千问办公2.0新增的自动任务。
资料空间与三端互联
千问办公2.0还提供了资料空间，把AI生成的表格、图片、HTML等产物集中放在一起。
想找之前做好的文件，就不用在对话列表里翻来翻去了。
你也可以把它当个网盘用，将项目方案、会议纪要、数据报表等本地文件都上传进去。
资料空间里的文件，也可以多选，然后基于这些文件发起一个新的对话，让Agent再帮你干活。
那我岂不是可以…
选中多份日报生成周报，再选中多份周报生成月报。
哎，谁有我天才啊。
此外，千问办公2.0还支持手机、电脑和网页端同步，任务进度、聊天记录和生成的文件都能接着看。
比如在电脑上发起一个任务，临时有事离开工位，可以用手机看看做到哪了，顺手补一句要求，不用重新开个对话、再解释一遍背景。
技术层面，千问办公2.0重构了自动化引擎，将任务调度迁移至云端。能在云端完成的任务，关了电脑也可以继续跑。
如果需要操作电脑里的文件或软件，电脑就得保持开机、联网。完成授权后，你人在外面，也可以通过手机远程下指令。
比如，让它在电脑里找一份文档，用钉钉发给客户；或者让它继续在电脑上做3D动画渲染，无需特意赶回工位。
Team Agent，办公AI进入多人协同模式
千问办公2.0把「协作」放在升级的中心，也带出了这次最重要的关键词：Team Agent。
Personal Agent主要围绕一个人的目标和偏好展开工作，比如Grok Bot，你可以让多个Bot并行处理任务，Bot之间还能传递信息、共享上下文、协调分工。
但当多名成员和Agent共同参与，产品需要处理的问题就越来越复杂——理解不同成员的分工，让大家能够基于已有的工作继续往下做。
这背后，是企业工作中一个很常见的问题：个人用AI提速之后，团队之间的交接仍然需要协调。
目前的主流办公Agent仍以服务个人为主，团队协作方式的变化相对有限。千问办公团队在技术博客中提出：下一代Agent需要进入团队协作的现场。
基于这一判断，千问办公还提出了企业级Team Agent应具备的五个特征：
进入团队，承担明确的角色。Agent需要理解项目上下文，有自己的职责和负责人，能够接住交办、推进任务，再把结果交回给人。
围绕同一份成果持续协作。人与AI可以在同一份文档、表格或应用上反复修改，从初稿到定稿持续接力，由人检查结果、作出决策。
按业务变化主动推进。当业务发生变化，Agent能够在授权范围内按规则先处理一步，把需要判断的事项交回负责人。这要求业务事件本身就能成为任务的入口，带上处理它所需的背景和规则。
持续在线，运行可管可控。Agent需要稳定地承接工作，同时让身份、权限、数据边界和执行记录清晰可查。任务交给AI处理后，团队仍要知道发生了什么，以及由谁负责。
连接企业已有的业务。专业应用可以进入AI工作平台，Agent能力也可以嵌入企业原有的CRM、ERP等系统，沿着已有流程参与工作。
这是一条持续演进的路线，千问办公2.0先从协作、人机共创与自动任务三个方向出发。
这种工作方式，在信息分散、需要反复汇总的业务里已经有了应用案例。
据官方介绍，银泰百货卡券运营团队的5名运营人员，过去需要到60多个门店群里逐一收集提报信息，核对后再回填表格。
用上千问办公2.0后，团队将这些门店群和一张AI表格关联到同一个协作空间，Agent可以跨群汇总信息，并自动更新表格。
门店继续在原来的群里提报，运营人员则减少了来回翻群、手动搬运信息的步骤。分散在群聊里的业务信息，也由此进入团队共同使用的表格，供后续工作继续使用。
企业级Agent未来的竞争方向，不再是卷完成一个通用任务的能力，而是比拼原子能力的融合，比谁能连接更多的办公工具、SaaS应用或企业内部OA系统。
群聊、Office已经长进了千问办公，按照产品团队的规划，千问办公后续还将探索接入更多SaaS应用、企业内部OA和专业工具，将企业已有的数据与流程更好地连接起来，并减少跨工具操作，让AI更深入地参与真实工作。
千问办公团队在博客中写道：
我们希望持续探索下一代Agent的演进方向：更主动，像人一样与团队共生协同。
个人效率是起点，而Team Agent是下一阶段的答案。
下一代企业办公入口，也要靠Agent深入业务流程、持续推动团队完成交付来赢得。

title: 成立四个月，融资过亿美金：TensorWorld物原科技要跑通“物理真实”路线
content:
< img id="wx_img" src="https://www.qbitai.com/wp-content/uploads/imgs/qbitai-logo-1.png" width="400" height="400">
TensorWorld物原科技在一个月内已拿到过亿美元融资
想象这样一个场景：一台人形机器人站在厨房里，面前是一只靠近桌沿的玻璃杯，伸出机械手想把杯子往里推——力道稍重，杯子滑落、坠地、碎裂。对人类而言，“杯子靠近桌边会掉下去，玻璃落地会碎”是近乎本能的预判；但对机器人而言，这种预判需要一套完整的物理逻辑：不仅要知道“眼前有什么”，还要理解“如果我这样做，接下来会发生什么”。
这正是当下AI行业最焦灼的战场之一，随着大语言模型推动智能在数字世界快速发展，AI的能力边界正在向物理世界延伸——具身智能、自动驾驶、工业仿真等等。但物理世界不按token出牌，它有自己的一套铁律：重力、摩擦、碰撞、流体……难度相比语言呈现指数级提升。
就在这条更难、更底层的赛道上，TensorWorld物原科技，一家成立仅四个月的初创公司，一个月内已经拿到过亿美元融资。资本押注的背后，是其“学术背景+技术路线+落地复现”能力带来的稀缺性。
行业需要解决什么问题？
当下，在公众的普遍认知里，AI已经非常聪明，不仅能写代码、找漏洞，甚至能攻克困扰人类数百年的数学难题，但要让机器人预测真实世界的物体轨迹并进行互动，却很难达到“可靠”的水平。原因在于，AI还没有理解物理规律，要让它从“软件界面”进入“物理世界”，这是绝对绕不开的关卡。
行业想要跨越这道鸿沟，面临着极度苛刻的条件：高保真的物理标注数据贵得惊人，一个工业级空气动力学仿真样本，往往需要数万 CPU 小时；在 100 个场景采集的数据很难泛化到 10000 个未知场景；仿真器很难完整复现真实世界的摩擦与形变，斯坦福 HAI 报告显示，机器人在软件仿真中的任务成功率可达 89.4%，但同一类任务在真实家庭环境中的成功率仅约 12.4%。
物原科技怎么解决这个问题？学术演进呈现清晰路径
目前，业内世界模型大致可归纳为
前者是行业主流，以视频生成为代表，目标是“看起来真实”
，优化的是帧间的像素合理性，优势是数据获取相对容易、画面逼真，多用于视频生成、数据工厂、场景预览、VLA前端感知。但机器人要在真实物理世界中可靠地执行任务，仅靠语言和视觉理解远远不够。
另一种范式越来越被行业认可，侧重以物理规律建模，目标是“推演更真实”
，优势是可验证、可测量、能支撑动作规划。传统工业仿真软件（如 MuJoCo、Isaac Sim）就是这条路线上的“手工派”——物理定律高度依赖工程师逐条手写，预测精确但昂贵，面对不规则形状、柔性体、流体时工程投入极高。
而物原科技，走的就是物理基础模型的路线，
他们提出“在张量世界中，构建物理真实”，目标是让模型从数据中学习物理世界的演化规律
，像人类一样达到“举一反三”的效果：
比如，原生Transformer缺乏时序拆解能力，怎么让模型正确理解物理世界中的“时间”？Autoformer大幅提升了长时序预测的精度，TimesNet又进一步让时间数据更加直观可视；再比如，怎么让模型理解“空间”？Uni3D将三维表征学习扩展到十亿参数规模，让模型对物体、几何与空间关系形成概念。
在此基础上，GeoPT则回答了这一赛道的灵魂之问——“物理直觉”能否被模型预训练出来？答案是可以，它创造性地让模型可以通过融合几何与合成动力学的预训练，获得可迁移的物理表征，在工业物理仿真任务中，该方法减少了20%至60%的有标签数据需求，并将收敛速度最高提升至2倍。Transolver又进一步让模型理解不规则空间中的受力、流动与形变，看懂更复杂的物理演化。EfficientZero则让智能体基于学习到的世界模型推演未来，并据此进行规划。
支撑这些前沿成果的，是物原创始团队横跨清华与 MIT 等国际顶尖学术机构的长期积淀。沿着
“时间演化—空间表征—物理规律—行动规划”
的递进主线，他们并非在堆砌孤立的论文，而是坚持从
物理规律出发，实现真正的“高阶物理智能”，
最终汇聚成了物理基座模型的完整轮廓。此外，物原团队此前还主导过亿级用户产品、管理过十万张加速卡的算力基础设施，具备丰厚的产业实战经验。如果说学术研究决定模型能力可以走多远，工程能力则决定模型能否用于真实业务场景，二者构成了物理基础模型的“一体两面”。
物原科技为什么被看好？物理驱动范式具备稀缺性
观察物原的技术路线，几乎对准了物理 AI 的三大痛点：在数据端，用合成动力学替代物理标签，大幅降低对昂贵真实数据的依赖；在泛化端，深度融合空间结构、时间演化与物理动力学，让模型自行涌现出通用的物理规律；在落地端，Autoformer、Transolver 等底层架构已被工业界广泛验证并采纳（如 NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo），化解AI在真实场景中落地的担忧。
“对物理系统的真正理解+世界模型驱动的规划能力+把前沿研究规模化落地的工程能力”这份交集的稀缺性，很快吸引了资本的关注。
自7月成立后，物原科技一个月内连续完成天使轮及天使+轮的过亿美金融资，其中天使轮由凯辉基金、红杉中国联合领投，IDG资本、鼎晖VGC、星连资本、蚂蚁集团跟投；天使+轮由蚂蚁集团、和玉资本、美团战投联合领投，达晨财智、蔚来资本、景和资本，以及多家老股东持续跟投。
这份融资名单也传递出许多信息：具有海量C端场景的美团战投，严肃工业场景的蚂蚁集团，以及自动驾驶场景的蔚来资本，都佐证了物原科技路线具备强烈的泛化特征，可匹配更广泛的行业需求。
世界模型赛道已经开始变得“拥挤”，但长时序预测的误差累积、仿真与真实的最后一段距离、评测标准的统一等问题仍然有待完善。物原科技的路线一旦走通，意味着模型真正具备理解世界运行、预判行动后果的能力，其价值不止于机器人或自动驾驶等单一场景，而有望成为Physical AI生态的底层标准与基座，为未来AI从数字世界走向物理世界铺平道路。

title: 英伟达机器人开源撞上Fable 5.2发布！Jim Fan：不是寒冬是夏天
content:
英伟达机器人开源撞上Fable 5.2发布！Jim Fan：不是寒冬是夏天
henry 发自 凹非寺
量子位 | 公众号 QbitAI
全体起立！时隔一年半，英伟达的新一代机器人基础模型终于来了！
刚刚，在今年奥斯汀举行的CoRL大会上，英伟达GEAR领导朱玉可和Jim Fan，搬出了新一代世界动作模型——
GR00T 2。
在时长1分半的官方demo中，GR00T 2可以拿剪刀裁标签、安装显卡、擦火柴、切香蕉做早餐、擦咖啡、收桌子、卖爆米花。
看下来，几乎是样样全能。从双手精细操作到全身移动，模型的任务范围几乎覆盖了机器人能力的各个方向。
而且，据朱玉可透露，GR00T2的模型、数据、仿真环境和数据采集硬件也将陆续开源。
目前，10万小时的人类数据已经率先开放。
咱一人来一句英伟达nb，不过分吧？
GR00T 2：扩展机器人基础模型的泛化、灵巧性与适应能力
作为一款世界动作模型，GR00T2能够同时预测未来画面与机器人动作。训练时，它把“世界将如何变化”和“机器人应当如何行动”放在一起学习。
发布会上，Jim Fan将其定位为一个反应够快、能够本地运行，同时既容易通过示范教会，也容易被推理模型引导的System 1（快系统）物理技能模型。
而放回GR00T 2内部，这就是朱玉可在推特上说的Xadapt跨本体适配。
简单来说，过去要教会一台机器人完成新任务，往往需要针对它的身体形态和控制方式，重新采集一批机器人示范数据。
X-Adapt则试图打破这层限制，人类或手持设备示范过的技能，可以直接迁移给没有练过这项任务的机器人。
具体来看，英伟达展示了三条路径。
1、从人类示范迁移到机器人。
研究人员佩戴动捕设备，示范如何放置、润湿滤纸。随后，双五指手Dexter就能完成同一任务。
整个过程中，没有采集该任务的机器人遥操作示范。仅凭人类示范，Dexter在20次试验中的成功率就达到65%。
2、从手持夹爪迁移到机械臂。
研究人员使用手持UMI夹爪，示范如何组装玩具自卸卡车。模型学习后，再将这项技能迁移到YAM机械臂上。
尽管UMI与YAM的夹爪形态不同，YAM仍能端到端完成最长约四分钟的组装任务，成功率达到60%。
同样的迁移路径，还被用于传送带分拣与抛掷、操作板拆解等任务。
3、从可穿戴外骨骼迁移到机器人灵巧手。
研究人员戴上DexUMI手部外骨骼，示范制作香蕉酸奶、舀取麦片。
模型利用这些数据微调后，机器人就能接手完成早餐任务，同样不需要额外采集这项任务的机器人遥操作示范。
总结来看，这三条路径指向同一个变化：同一项技能，不必总是在每一种机器人上重新示范一遍。
当然，跨本体迁移并不意味着完全不需要机器人数据。
在人类动捕和UMI路径中，目标机器人仍会提供与具体任务无关的数据，让模型熟悉自身的身体结构、运动方式和控制空间。新任务的示范，则可以来自更容易采集的人类操作。
这也是GR00T2技术报告所强调的方向，扩展机器人基础模型的泛化、灵巧性与适应能力。
迁移之外，GR00T 2也展示了通过少量机器人示范提高执行精度的能力。
在另一组Dexter-50评测中，模型的零样本平均成功率为40%；每项任务提供一次示范后，成功率提高到71%；提供五次示范后，则达到95%。
更关键的是，这五次示范合计不足三分钟。随后，只需要在单张RTX5090上进行约30分钟的LoRA微调，就能得到适配对应任务的模型。
在实际调用方面，英伟达也紧跟潮流，开放了WAM API。
通过API，推理模型可以负责拆解任务、检查执行进度，再将具体的物理技能交给GR00T2执行。
换句话说，GR00T2不仅可以自己完成技能，还能成为上层智能体调用的物理执行模块。
那么，问题来了：英伟达，你咋这么nb？
40 万小时人类视频，怎么变成机器人的动手能力？
咱一个一个来说。X-Adapt背后，首先是一座数据金字塔。GR00T2的预训练混合了三类数据：
402,730小时人类第一视角视频；
10,184小时手持UMI演示，覆盖2,897项任务；
23,500小时机器人遥操作数据。
不难看出，人类视频的规模远大于另外两类。这意味着，机器人的学习材料不再局限于人工遥操作采集的动作轨迹，而是进一步扩展到大量真实的人类活动：
人怎样拿起工具、移动物体、完成装配，以及一次动作之后，周围场景会发生怎样的变化。
UMI和可穿戴设备负责补充更直接的操作轨迹，机器人遥操作数据则帮助模型学习不同身体对应的运动与控制方式。
为了验证人类视频究竟能不能帮助机器人干活？团队还专门做了一组规模实验。
他们分别使用不含人类视频、1%、10%和全部人类视频的数据训练模型，再在72项Dexter任务上评估。
结果显示，随着人类视频数据增加，真实机器人上的平均任务进度从50%提高到70%。
这组实验给出了一个相当直接的答案：大规模人类经验，不只是丰富模型的视觉知识，也能转化成机器人在真实任务中的执行进展。
为了吃下这些数据，在模型方面，GR00T2则接收语言指令、多视角相机画面和机器人状态，通过同一个扩散Transformer，联合预测未来视频与动作序列。
最后，围绕GR00T2，英伟达还在把数据采集、处理、训练、仿真验证和实际部署接成一套完整工具链。
采集端，是UMI、DexUMI等设备。它们让研究人员直接记录人类操作，尤其是那些传统遥操作很难自然完成的灵巧动作。
数据端，包括Human-1M与Flora。前者提供人类第一视角视频，首批10万小时子集已经公开；后者支持数据整理、描述性标注和自动评估。
仿真端，则有SimFoundry。它可以从真实场景重建任务环境，用于策略测试、数据生成和技能开发。
执行端，则由不同模型和组件分工完成。
ASPIRE将机器人模型与代码技能组织起来，支持任务执行和错误恢复。面向人形机器人，Turbo使用更轻量的网络和更紧凑的视频表示，降低预测开销。
在G1的机载Jetson Thor上，Turbo单次预测耗时为124毫秒；SONIC则运行在另一块Jetson Orin上，以50Hz进行全身控制。
前者生成运动计划，后者把计划转化为持续的身体动作，让机器人在伸手、弯腰和搬运时维持协调。
这样一来，开发者拿到GR00T2后，不仅能调用模型本身，还能沿着配套工具链采集自己的数据、适配自己的任务、在仿真中验证技能，最后将其部署到真实机器人上。
这也是英伟达此次发布更值得关注的地方：它开放的已经不只是一款机器人模型，而是从数据采集、模型训练到技能调用和实际执行的一整套开发体系。
One more thing
在CoRL的现场演讲里，Jim Fan说：
“Astra没有打碎我们的梦想，它打破的是我们的围墙。”
“这不是寒冬，这是机器人的夏天。”
虽然话是这么说不错，但今天发布的Claude Fable 5.2，在RoboDojo上的表现也着实有点，来给机器人学上课的意思。
在Anthropic公布的RoboDojo Sim仿真双臂测试中，采用相同运行框架、各模型最高可用推理强度，Fable 5.2得分 64.9%，GPT-6 Astra为29.8%。
要不，下次「后会友期」，大模型队和具身模型队也来报个名？

title: 达卯科技与浦东环保能源战略合作，黎明智算中心算电协同平台启动
content:
达卯科技与浦东环保能源战略合作，黎明智算中心算电协同平台启动
加速东部城市型智算中心向E-AIDC演进
近日，达卯科技与上海浦东环保能源发展有限公司（简称“浦东环保能源”）正式签署战略合作协议。双方将围绕数据中心节能优化与智慧管控、电力市场化运营、算电协同智能化体系建设、协同生态共建四大领域开展深度布局，共同推动算电协同场景落地与产业赋能。
作为本次战略合作的首个落地成果，达卯科技为国家级算电协同试点浦东新区黎明智算中心打造算电协同平台，推动双方合作从战略规划快速落地见效。
全面战略合作，共同促进算电协同行业发展
浦东环保能源是上海浦发集团全资组建的国有独资企业，作为集团绿色低碳及算力服务产业的核心承载主体，深耕环保与新能源领域，已构建“发电-储能-配电-用能-交易”全链条能源运营模式，是浦东新区算电协同与绿色算力产业的重要实践平台。
达卯科技作为算电协同领域核心软件与全周期价值运营服务商，以自研垂类能源大模型与智能体集群为技术底座，具备从项目咨询规划、算电协同AI产品集成应用、运维运营一体化的全周期服务能力。
根据协议，双方将发挥各自优势、分阶段开展全面战略合作：
数据中心节能优化与智慧管控建设：共建安全可靠、绿色高效、智慧可控的数据中心能源运营体系，打造一体化智慧能源管控调度能力，优化供冷运行策略、完善安全保障机制，实现用能可视化、运营数字化。
电力市场化运营与辅助决策：联合推进虚拟电厂体系搭建、资源聚合、平台运营与市场化交易业务，依托交易策略优化、市场申报支撑、电价预测辅助决策等全链条技术赋能，全面盘活能源资产、提升市场化增值收益。
算电协同智能化体系与通用市场化平台：依托达卯科技智能算法与能源大模型技术，联合构建算力、电力、能耗资源一体化智能调度体系，打造标准化、可复用的行业通用平台，沉淀可复制推广的算电协同标杆解决方案。
算电深度协同生态与能力共建：探索数据中心深度资源协同创新模式，持续开展技术储备与方案研究，拓展战略合作的深度与广度，构建长效算电协同产业生态。
黎明智算中心启动算电协同平台建设
作为战略合作首个落地项目，黎明智算中心算电协同平台建设已正式启动。
黎明智算中心是上海浦东北片区首个万卡级算力集群，同时为国家级算电协同试点项目。设计总功率18兆瓦，项目创新采用生物质绿电直供、余热制冷与LNG相变余冷梯级利用综合技术，是超低PUE绿色智算中心标杆。
本次算电协同平台建设涵盖平台功能开发、数据采集对接、实施部署与运营培训多个模块，将落地智算中心资源监控、运行分析、负荷预测、协同调度及系统管理等核心功能。
平台建成后，将实现园区用能全链路数字化管控、蓄冷罐等柔性资源聚合监控，以及供冷系统协同调度策略支撑，在保障园区安全稳定运行前提下，持续优化PUE与能耗治理水平，并为后续参与电能量交易、电力辅助服务等市场化业务筑牢技术底座。
示范引领，加速东部城市型智算中心向E-AIDC演进
当前，东部城市智算中心普遍面临电网容量约束、能耗指标趋紧的现实挑战，算电协同已从成本优化选项，转变为产业高质量发展的核心路径。
此次达卯科技与浦东环保能源的战略合作，是国有能源运营平台与AI科技企业的深度联手。双方以黎明智算中心为实践起点，将能源工程运营经验与AI节能智控技术深度融合，探索可复制、可推广的城市型智算中心算电协同运营模式。
这一合作将推动智算中心从传统被动用电负荷，向可调节、可交易、可增值的主动能源运营节点升级，为东部城市智算中心规模化落地算电协同提供示范样本，助力E-AIDC能源驱动型智算中心范式从理念走向更广泛的产业实践。

title: Berwick Bank B offshore wind project expected to support 2,600 UK jobs
content:
Berwick Bank B offshore wind project expected to support 2,600 UK jobs TGS 4C | 4C Offshore News
Berwick Bank B offshore wind project expected to support 2,600 UK jobs
SSE has announced that the 1.4 GW Berwick
offshore wind project is expected to create more than 2,600 jobs in the
UK. The large-scale offshore wind farm will not only support renewable
energy ambitions but also boost industrial growth while supporting skilled
regional jobs.
The announcement follows news that Siemens Energy has been selected as
the preferred supplier of wind turbines and substations for the project.
However, the agreement remains subject to a final investment decision.
Darren Davidson, Managing Director of Siemens Energy UK & Ireland,
said: “While the project remains subject to final approvals and contract
award, we are proud to be working alongside SSE as it progresses this nationally
significant development.”
According to the announcement, the jobs will span manufacturing, engineering,
project delivery and service roles, totalling 2,677 skilled positions.
Siemens Energy will also utilise its established operations across the
UK, which currently support 2,222 jobs, including roles in wind and grid
technologies and at its wind turbine blade factory in Hull.
SSE and Siemens Energy will support an additional 455 engineering, project
delivery and service jobs, bringing the total to more than 3,000.
UK Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh said: “This is another vote of confidence
in British homegrown clean energy."
“Investment in offshore wind and clean power is creating quality jobs
and rebuilding industry, while delivering the clean power we need to lower
bills and reach net zero.”
Scottish Energy Minister Stephen Gethins said: “I warmly welcome the news
that SSE’s Berwick Bank project will now support almost 1,000 jobs in
Scotland, including the 130 new roles based in Glasgow and Montrose that
have been announced today.”

title: Cadeler sign exclusivity agreement for UK offshore wind farm
content:
Cadeler has announced that it has signed an exclusivity agreement for turbine
and foundation installation work at a large-scale UK offshore wind farm.
The client has yet to be disclosed, however, the announcement states that
the agreement demonstrates the importance of securing installation capacity
early, especially for larger-scale developments.
The company has confirmed that it will use A-Class and O-Class vessels
to carry out foundation installation work, while the turbine installation
campaign will be undertaken using one of its P-Class vessels.
Mikkel Gleerup, CEO of Cadeler, commented: “We are very pleased to announce
this significant project, which is another important endorsement of the
capabilities of our fleet, the experience of our people and Cadeler’s
ability to deliver increasingly large and complex offshore wind projects.”
Cadeler currently operates one of the largest offshore wind installation
fleets globally, consisting of eleven installation vessels, with an additional
three newbuilds scheduled for delivery. This enables the company to support
larger-scale and more complex projects.
According to the announcement, its work on the project is expected to begin
around 2030.

title: European Commission approves support scheme for First Princess Elisabeth Zone project
content:
European Commission approves support scheme for First Princess Elisabeth Zone project TGS 4C | 4C Offshore News
European Commission approves support scheme for First Princess Elisabeth Zone project
The European Commission has officially approved the state aid mechanism
for the first plot in Belgium's Princess Elisabeth Zone (PEZ 1).
The approval removes the final barrier to relaunching the tender process.
The previous tender was paused in 2025 due to a range of legal, financial
and technical concerns.
Following the suspension, the federal government revised the tender framework
in an effort to provide greater certainty for developers and investors
while maintaining competition. The updated structure includes a two-sided
Contract for Difference (CfD) support mechanism.
The updated framework also extends the project's construction period from
four years to five years. Belgian Energy Minister Mathieu Bihet said the
Commission's decision was the final element needed to relaunch the tender.
“This is an important step which demonstrates the quality of the work
delivered by the teams and the robustness of the framework we have built,”
said the Federal Minister of Energy, Mathieu Bihet.
The Princess Elisabeth Zone forms part of Belgium's offshore wind expansion
plans and is intended to support the country's energy security and economic
competitiveness.

title: Hornsea 3 turbine components reach ABLE Seaton Port
content:
Ørsted has announced that components for the 2.9 GW Hornsea
3 offshore wind farm
are currently at ABLE Seaton Port in north east England, where they will
be loaded out for offshore installation operations.
The wind turbine components include blades, nacelles and tower sections.
According to the company, the turbine towers will be delivered in four
sections and assembled on site.
Once installed, each turbine tower will stand 130 metres tall, while the
turbine blades will measure 115 metres in length.
The project is expected to be completed by the end of 2027 and generate
enough renewable electricity to power 3.3 million UK homes, supporting
the UK's net zero goals.
Ørsted said that, through its agreement with ABLE Seaton Port and its contractors,
around 70 new workers have been employed to support the project. The company
have said Hornsea 3 is expected to support up to 5,000 jobs during the
construction phase.

title: RWE and KKR finalise financing for 2.8GW Vanguard offshore wind projects
content:
RWE and KKR have announced that they will jointly deliver the Vanguard
and Vanguard
offshore wind projects, located 50 and 80 kilometres off the Norfolk coast.
The Vanguard offshore wind farms are expected to have a combined capacity
of 2.8 GW, enough to power 3 million U.K. homes. The projects have the
potential to support the local economy by creating long-term jobs and reinforcing
East Anglia's position as an offshore wind hub.
The announcement follows the companies' joint venture transaction announced
in January 2026, under which KKR acquired a 50% equity stake in each project.
The agreement combines RWE's offshore wind development and operational
expertise with KKR's capital resources and global infrastructure investment
experience.
According to the announcement, the wind farms require around £12 billion
to support construction and associated infrastructure. Funding has been
backed by equity commitments from RWE and KKR, while additional financing
has been secured from a consortium of international lenders.
Both projects have now reached financial close, securing £11.1 billion
in non-recourse project financing facilities and a further £1.7 billion
in ancillary facilities from a group of 35 international banks. The financing
marks a milestone as the largest project financing package ever secured
for U.K. offshore wind.
U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham said: "This major investment in U.K.
renewables is a vote of confidence in building in Britain. And it is great
news for billpayers because every turbine we put up is power under British
control, not at the mercy of events on the other side of the world."
TGS | 4C Senior Analyst Jordan May commented: "RWE and KKR's financial
close is a great step for the UK, marking the first Allocation Round 7
project to make FID, and a large amount of capacity getting ready to come
online before 2030."
"The UK has 10.5 GW under construction some of which is expected to
complete construction soon. Adding on another 2.76 GW will allow UK waters
to stay busy, keeping the industry well stocked with active UK projects.
It also goes to show industry resilience to global geopolitical events
which challenge the global investment environment."

title: Cadillac Vistiq Sport Review Tested
content:
Charging
Automotive & Mobility
Design & Manufacturing
We spent a week testing Cadillac's electric SUV on Tesla chargers and busy highways, with mixed results.
November 11, 2026
4 Min Read
Cadillac Vistiq EV.
General Motors Co.
At a Glance
NACS port lets Vistiq charge at Tesla stations, but cable length creates parking challenges
Supercruise handles open highways well, but hesitates in dense, aggressive traffic
Stiff suspension and big wheels mean the Vistiq rides rougher than classic Cadillac luxury
A week in the $83,256 (as tested, including destination) 2027
Cadillac
Vistiq Sport provided more time with General Motors’ Supercruise driver assistance system and our first use of Tesla Supercharger charging stations with the Vistiq’s new
North American Charging System (NACS)
charging port.
The car’s dual-motor all-wheel-drive system is rated at 615 horsepower and 650 lb.-ft. of torque, which is obviously more than sufficient for a mid-sized three-row family SUV.
NACS Charging
The EPA estimates the Vistiq’s 102-kilowatt-hour NCMA lithium-ion battery pack provides 300 miles of driving range on a charge, but in recent mild fall weather, our test vehicle’s computer predicted 311 miles. The EPA turned out to be right, as a 233-mile trip consumed 240 miles of the forecast range.
Angling the Vistiq into the Supercharger station so the short charging cable will reach the car's side-mounted charge port. DAN CARNEY
For the 2027 model year, the Vistiq gains a NACS charging port, and it provided our first chance to visit a Tesla Supercharger station. On arrival at the row of 8 charging stations, there were two Tesla Model Ss on hand. Fortunately, they were on one end of the row, because I quickly realized that the stubby little charge cable on the Tesla chargers is too short to reach the Vistiq’s charge port on the driver’s side front fender.
This is a convenient location for home charging, and it works fine at other public charging stations, but the shorter Tesla cables are designed to reach only the rear-mounted charge ports on the company’s own cars, when they are backed into the space in front of the charger. To charge the Vistiq, I had to parallel park across several spaces in front of the chargers to get the port close enough.
The 67 kWh of juice cost $41.65, and charging from a 20% state of charge to 75% took 31 minutes even though the battery was preconditioned before starting. The car promised to charge to 80% in 30 minutes, but it began tapering the charge rate early in the process, so the initial 166 kW rate slowed to only 80 kW by a 70% SoC. Then the car predicted that it would take 40 minutes to reach 80%, but the prospect of additional slowing caused me to pull the plug at 75%.
Supercruise
The Vistiq’s Supercruise system works as advertised on the highway, though it continues to struggle with the multilane mayhem of roads like Interstate 95. In terms of providing adaptive cruise control and managing stop-and-go traffic while automatically following the road, the system works well.
But in terms of interacting with other cars, Supercruise has the awkward timing and lack of foresight of driver’s ed student. The system can change lanes automatically on its own or when the driver prompts it by activating the turn signal. In either case, it is far too timid and slow in initiating the lane change.
This is surely meant as a conservative, safe-driving approach, but it has the effect of more frequently cutting off fast-approaching drivers in the lane being entered. That’s because Supercruise waits too long to realize that it wants to overtake slower traffic in its current lane. By the time it decides to make the change, it often has to slow to match the speed of that slow-moving car.
Now, when it moves into the next lane, where the traffic is moving faster, it is going more slowly than it would have been going if it had made the merge before catching up to the car that was in the way. This is exacerbated by Supercruise being slow to actually then make the merge into the other lane.
Nature abhors a vacuum, and a traffic opening is the same, attracting drivers to fill open space. These delays invite others to move into that space, at which point Supercruise stumbles belatedly toward the rapidly closing spot, cutting off the other car.
The system is also bad at recognizing when other drivers are behaving aggressively. In the belated merge situation, there are drivers who won’t yield. Supercruise seems pretty willing to collide with them, or come closer to doing so that I’m comfortable with, so I found myself overriding lane changes and/or braking to avoid collisions caused by its inept decision-making. This is supposed to make driving more relaxing, remember?
Supercruise seems very useful on lightly traveled highways, but at this point, using it on congested roads filled with aggressive drivers seems more trouble than it is worth.
Road Manners
The Vistiq rolls on 21-inch wheels, which are not absurdly huge by contemporary standards. But the low-profile tires they use, combined with the stiff spring rate needed to support the car’s heavy battery pack combine to transmit harsh road impacts directly to the cabin.
Rolling on a rural highway that seemingly suffered heat-related asphalt buckling made it clear that the Vistiq does not ride like a Cadillac. The heat buckles had been shaved off, leaving behind stripes of asphalt patches across the lane at regular intervals, sort of the tarmac equivalent of concrete expansion joints. These hammered the Vistiq’s occupants relentlessly, leaving us to fantasize about the Cadillac road yachts of yore, which would have absorbed these road imperfections imperceptibly.

title: IEA: Batteries Move to Center of Renewable Energy Growth
content:
Battery Applications
Stationary Batteries
Market Analysis
Industry Trends
IEA says batteries are central to renewable growth, with storage reshaping solar economics, grid flexibility, and energy resilience worldwide today.
November 10, 2026
4 Min Read
Battery energy storage system for residential use with solar panel on roof.
2229678200/iStock / Getty Images Plus
Battery storage was often framed as a complementary technology to renewable energy rather than central to it. Solar and wind attracted most of the attention, but the balance is now shifting. The International Energy Agency’s
Renewables 2026
report suggests batteries, especially behind-the-meter systems installed at homes and businesses, are becoming increasingly important to how renewable electricity is used, valued, and integrated into power systems.
Recent coverage in
Battery Technology
also reflects this shift. The article “
7 Residential Battery Storage Systems Worth Buying in 2026
” shows that home batteries are increasingly positioned as part of an integrated energy system, with newer models combining storage, controls, and EV charging. The piece “
Understanding Base Power’s role in energy storage solutions
” similarly highlights how distributed batteries are linked to grid reliability and cost savings. Together, the articles suggest that batteries are viewed less as stand-alone products and more as a bridge between the home and the wider power system.
Related:
Why Solid-State Batteries Matter for Space
Rapid growth changes the scale of the story
The IEA’s projections indicate that behind-the-meter battery storage is moving beyond a niche market. The report says installed capacity is set to “expand more than fivefold, exceeding 670 GWh by 2031,” while power capacity reaches roughly 290 GW. Over 2026-2031, more than 550 GWh of energy storage capacity is expected to be added.
Those figures suggest storage is no longer peripheral to renewable deployment. It is becoming part of the infrastructure that supports the next phase of market growth. As renewable electricity takes a larger share of total generation, systems need more flexibility to absorb and shift that power. Batteries are increasingly providing part of that flexibility.
Global installed behind-the-meter energy storage capacity (left) and power storage capacity (right) by segment, 2020-2031. Courtesy of IEA.
According to the report, declining battery costs are improving the case for households and businesses to install storage alongside solar. In many markets, batteries now offer a clearer route to self-consumption, cost savings, and reduced exposure to high retail electricity prices.
Behind-the-meter storage gains strategic importance
Behind-the-meter batteries differ from utility-scale storage because they are installed on the customer side of the meter. The IEA notes that behind-the-meter systems allow households and businesses to “increase self-consumption, lower electricity costs and reduce peak demand.” That combination is important at both the consumer and system level. For the user, storage can improve the value of solar generation and reduce reliance on expensive electricity purchased during peak periods. For the grid, widespread battery adoption can ease pressure on networks and reduce demand spikes.
Related:
Robot Dogs & Mobile Chargers Power Up Detroit's Smart Parking Test Bed
Commercial demand broadens the market
Another sign that batteries are becoming central to renewable growth is the changing customer mix. Residential batteries still account for the majority of behind-the-meter storage capacity today, but the IEA expects commercial deployment to accelerate sharply over the next several years.
According to the report, “growth is increasingly balanced across customer segments,” with commercial storage expected to account for almost half of global additions during 2026-2031. That marks a meaningful shift from the previous period, when residential systems dominated more clearly.
Global net additions of behind-the-meter energy storage capacity (left) by segment, 2020-2031 and (right) by country and segment, 2026-2031. Courtesy of IEA.
This matters because broader commercial adoption suggests the market is maturing. Storage is no longer limited mainly to early adopters in the residential sector. Businesses are increasingly seeing value in batteries for peak shaving, load shifting, and energy cost management. In some markets, batteries are also becoming part of virtual power plant models and demand-response participation.
Solar-plus-storage becomes more common
The growing connection between batteries and distributed solar is another reason storage is moving closer to the center of the renewable story. The IEA projects that annual residential battery additions will rise from the equivalent of 13% of rooftop solar PV additions in 2025 to more than 35% by 2031.
Related:
Public-Private Collaboration Advances Nuclear Power for Space Exploration
That trend shows batteries are being deployed faster than rooftop solar itself in many markets. The report states that in mature rooftop solar markets, battery adoption is “becoming the norm rather than the exception.” Germany illustrates this change clearly: around 80% of new residential solar PV systems installed in 2025 included battery storage.
The implication is straightforward. Renewable generation alone is no longer the full measure of progress. Increasingly, the ability to store and shift that electricity is part of the value proposition.
Annual residential storage additions and residential electricity prices in selected markets, 2021-2025. Courtesy of IEA.
Batteries are increasingly influencing how efficiently renewable electricity can be consumed, monetized, and integrated into the system. As costs fall and deployment expands across residential and commercial markets, battery storage is becoming more central. It is helping renewable power become more flexible, reliable, and practical for everyday use. That shift is making storage a bigger part of how energy systems are built and managed.

title: Data Center Power Demand Is Set to Surge, Raising New Climate Challenges: BloombergNEF | BloombergNEF
content:
PRESS RELEASE
Data Centers
November 11, 2026
KEY TAKEAWAYS
A new report from BloombergNEF, commissioned by Bloomberg Philanthropies indicates that data center electricity demand is set to almost quadruple to 2,354 terawatt-hours by 2035, equivalent to 7% of global electricity demand.
The rush for “speed to power” is pushing some developers toward on-site gas. BNEF has tracked 181GW of announced gas-fired generation proposed alongside data centers, with more than 90% in the US.
Policies can help limit near-term emissions impacts, but the appropriate approach varies by market. Faster grid connections, financial commitments, flexible connections, special zones and clean-power procurement are among the approaches reviewed, while continued power-system decarbonization remains vital.
New York, November 11, 2026
– Data center power demand is set to surge as developers seek to bring new computing capacity online quickly. BloombergNEF (BNEF) expects data center electricity demand to almost quadruple to 2,354 terawatt-hours by 2035, equivalent to 7% of global electricity consumption, according to a new report commissioned by Bloomberg Philanthropies.
Powering the Data Center Boom: How Grid Policy Can Deliver Clean Power Faster
finds that grid constraints in the US and Europe are delaying new connections for large loads, while the financial rewards for energizing quickly are driving some developers to build on-site gas-fired power as they await a grid connection. BNEF has tracked 181GW of announced gas-fired generation proposed alongside data centers, more than 90% of which is in the US. The announced pipeline varies widely in maturity and timing and should be viewed as an indication of potential scale rather than a forecast of what will ultimately be built.
If all announced on-site gas plants proposed for US data centers were built and operated at the assumptions used by BNEF, they would emit about 345 million metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent a year. That would be 152MtCO2e more than if the associated data center capacity were supplied by average US grid electricity, an amount equivalent to 10% of US power-sector emissions in 2025. Although many of these projects are intended to supply power while data centers await a grid connection, BNEF finds that once they are online, the economics could encourage them to continue generating energy, creating a longer-term fossil-fuel lock-in risk beyond the annual emissions.
In developed markets such as the US and Europe, ensuring new data centers are grid-connected is the more sustainable option, making faster grid connections important to limiting near-term emissions impacts and fossil-fuel lock-in risk. Continuing to decarbonize the power system in parallel also remains vital.The report reviews policies across 17 markets that aim to accelerate the grid connection process. The policy landscape is still emerging and while many efforts should reduce waiting times for connections, there is currently limited empirical evidence to demonstrate which will be most effective.
Mark Daly, Head of Data Centers and Emerging Tech at BloombergNEF said, “The extraordinary economics around AI are making speed to power one of the most important priorities for  defining constraints on data center developers. The climate outcome will depend not only on how much electricity these facilities use, but on how quickly grids can connect them and whether power systems add cleaner generation alongside that demand.”
In emerging markets, the challenges of mitigating the climate impact of data centers differs. BNEF finds that, where power systems remain heavily reliant on coal, grid-connected data centers can be even worse than those powered by on-site gas. This highlights how much more central it is in these markets to enable more clean generation alongside sources of new power demand.
The four emerging markets examined in the report are:
BNEF expects almost all incremental generation needed to meet data center demand through 2035 to come from renewables. Large consumers buy directly with renewable generators, and new data center demand could absorb some renewable generation that is currently curtailed, although transmission remains a constraint.
Data center electricity demand is expected to rise from 11TWh in 2025 to 91TWh in 2035. Existing coal plants supply much of the additional electricity in the near term under BNEF’s Economic Transition Scenario, but data centers can procure clean power through bilateral and captive projects, and companies are already backing new solar and wind capacity.
Indonesia:
Coal and gas supplied 82% of state utility PLN’s on-grid power in 2025. Current rules do not allow data centers to contract directly with independent renewable generators, limiting their ability to link corporate demand clearly to new clean-power capacity.
Malaysia
: Data center electricity demand is set to rise from 7TWh in 2025 to 45TWh by 2035. Additional demand is expected to increase the use of existing coal and gas plants in the near term, while continued demand growth is likely to result in new gas capacity and coal life extensions over the longer term. Data centers can contract with third-party renewable generators and are already supporting new solar projects, although network charges can affect the economics of these contracts.
The report finds that policies to accelerate grid connections can help limit the near-term emissions impact and fossil-fuel lock-in risk in developed markets, but the challenge differs across markets. Continued power-system decarbonization and frameworks that allow data centers to support additional clean power will also be important as data center electricity demand grows.

title: AMD Launches Epyc SP7, Helion as AI Rack Demand Rises
content:
AMD said Tuesday that its sixth-generation Epyc SP7 server processor is now generally available and that hardware makers have begun shipping servers powered by the new chip.
The company also said the first Helion racks for agentic AI, which hardware vendors build from an AMD blueprint, will become available throughout this month.
The new SP7 processor, which features up to 256 cores, is the first of
four sixth-generation Epyc CPUs
to become available. The other three are expected in 2027, AMD said. The broader family of sixth-generation processors, much of which is code-named “Venice,” is designed for enterprise, cloud, high-performance computing, and AI workloads, including agentic AI.
AMD said it is seeing strong demand for the new chip. During the company’s third-quarter earnings call last week, AMD Chair and CEO Lisa Su said early demand for Venice is the strongest AMD has seen for any new generation of Epyc processors.
Related:
Google Adds TPU 8tx, 8i Max for Enterprise AI
Su said AMD began revenue shipments of Venice during the third quarter and that hardware makers have committed to more than 240 Venice platforms, 20% more than the number committed for Turin, AMD’s fifth-generation Epyc chip.
AMD is working to capture more market share in CPUs, GPUs, and overall AI infrastructure as it competes with rivals amid surging AI demand.
AMD is directly challenging market leader Nvidia in GPUs and rack-scale systems, while Nvidia is
taking on
AMD with its own CPU.
has also introduced its own Arm-based CPU to compete with Intel and AMD’s x86 processors, and cloud providers AWS,
Google Cloud
, and Microsoft Azure have built their own custom AI accelerators and Arm-based CPUs.
Sixth-Gen Epyc Targets AI Infrastructure as Helion Comes Online
During the earnings call, Su said Venice delivers significantly better performance per watt, per core, and per dollar than any other x86 or Arm server CPU.
AMD said systems based on the new Epyc SP7 processor deliver up to 3.7 times more performance than an Nvidia Vera CPU-based system and up to 2.2 times the performance of an Intel Xeon 6980P system.
Agentic AI is driving demand for server CPUs, which play three distinct roles for the emerging workload: general-purpose services, GPU host nodes, and agent sandboxes. While GPUs handle inference, organizations still need a large number of CPUs to orchestrate the workflow, from invoking tools to retrieving data.
AMD introduced Helion in October as an open rack-scale design for agentic AI. Hardware partners include Dell Technologies, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, Lenovo, Supermicro, and Cisco. Helion racks, built for agentic AI, are different from AMD’s Helios racks, which are designed for large-scale inference, frontier model training, and fine-tuning.
Related:
Nvidia Probes Huang Ties as AI Industry Weighs the Fallout
AMD said Helion will come in three versions:
Helion Liquid, a CPU-only, liquid-cooled rack designed to operate side by side with a Helios rack for large-scale agentic AI deployments;
Helion Air, a CPU-only rack designed to expand agent capacity within existing air-cooled data centers; and
AMD Helion Air Inference, an air-cooled rack that combines CPUs and GPUs for inference.
AMD also said Meta is preparing to deploy sixth-generation AMD Epyc CPU-based platforms at scale and that Microsoft Azure’s Azure HDv2 service for AI data processing is now in preview.
Why Venice Matters to Enterprise Data Centers
Matt Kimball, vice president and principal analyst at Moor Insights & Strategy, said Venice is an important launch for AMD and for enterprises.
Enterprise CIOs have fixed power budgets in their data centers and need infrastructure that supports not only traditional workloads today, but also agentic AI in the years ahead, Kimball said. With up to 256 cores, Venice lets companies run traditional workloads on fewer servers, freeing up space for AI infrastructure.
Related:
Nvidia, AMD Commit $4B to Meta AI Buildout
Servers running sixth-generation Epyc processors today are also well suited to support agentic workloads in the future because of the CPU’s high core count and large cache and memory, Kimball noted.
“It’s huge for those enterprise organizations that are in the beginning stages of the AI-ification of their business,” he said.

title: The Rural Shift in Data Center Development
content:
Traditionally, key considerations when selecting a data center site have included access to power, proximity to end-user concentrations, and the availability of high-performance network infrastructure. Those factors help explain why data centers have historically been built
in or near urban areas
rather than in remote regions.
Recent developments, however, suggest that this pattern is changing.
Two-thirds
of new US data center projects are targeting rural locations, marking a shift away from the longstanding concentration of facilities in major hubs such as Northern Virginia, Texas, and California.
The change is not limited to the United States. Hyperscalers are also evaluating remote parts of
South America
as potential locations for the next generation of data centers.
That shift raises two questions: Why are remote regions gaining prominence as data center sites, and does this represent a lasting change in site-selection strategy?
Related:
Brazil’s Data Center Growth Pushes Beyond São Paulo
Why Rural Sites Are Gaining Appeal
Rural areas present distinct challenges as data center sites. They are often farther from end users, which can increase latency, and power and network infrastructure may be less developed or located farther away.
At the same time, rural settings can offer advantages that may outweigh those drawbacks for some operators.
One of the biggest is land availability.
Securing enough land
for a data center in or near an urban area can be difficult and expensive because undeveloped parcels are limited. In many rural markets, that constraint is less severe.
Community opposition
may also be more limited in less densely developed areas.
Permitting
can be simpler, too, because lower levels of surrounding development often mean fewer barriers to new construction.
Power Constraints Are Reshaping Site Selection
Another factor behind the shift toward less developed areas is the growing importance of
on-site power generation
In a market where public power grids, including those in wealthy, highly developed regions, cannot always meet the capacity needs of new data centers, operators are increasingly exploring self-generated power. That can include dedicated generation assets or on-site plants. From that perspective, limited access to existing grid infrastructure in remote regions becomes less of a constraint.
Fiber Is Still a Challenge, but a Manageable One
On-site power does not solve every problem. Data centers still need access to high-performance network infrastructure, which, in most cases, means fiber-optic cables. Many rural areas currently have limited fiber access.
Related:
Virginia Tops AI Data Center Readiness Ranking as Smaller Markets Advance
Still, networking may be easier to address than power. Extending fiber is typically less expensive and less complex than building long-distance power infrastructure or developing major on-site generation capacity. In many cases, if existing fiber is available within a few hundred miles of a proposed site, connecting to it can be economically viable.
Rural Data Centers Are Not New, but the Scale Is
Although nearly
nine-tenths
of existing data centers remain concentrated in developed areas, the idea of placing facilities in rural regions is not new.
Amazon, for example, explored the feasibility of data centers in Chile and Argentina
more than eight years ago
, and the discussion of rural data center development dates back at least a decade.
What is different now is the level of execution. Over the past few years, operators have begun breaking ground on rural projects on a greater scale, driven by changing dynamics around power sourcing, land availability, and community response.
Why the Shift to Rural Data Centers May Continue
The factors that make rural locations more attractive are unlikely to disappear soon, suggesting that the industry will continue to expand into less-developed areas.
That does not mean every new data center will be built far from cities.
Urban sites
will remain important for facilities that require ultra-low latency or whose scale does not justify the infrastructure investment needed to support a remote site.
Related:
EMEA Data Center Expansion Faces a Delivery Test
Even so, rural development appears to be shifting from exception to mainstream strategy. If constraints on power, land, and local opposition persist, a larger share of the industry’s next wave of large-scale projects is likely to be sited outside traditional metro hubs.

title: Winning Data Center Bids Starts with the Investment Tax Credit
content:
Picture two proposals for a data center bid. The pricing is similar. The timelines are similar. One covers the construction scope. The other shows how the project can be structured not just on a blueprint but on a tax return to unlock additional financial value.
For an owner weighing the full economics of a data center investment, the difference can be compelling.
For years, apart from the largest industry players, few other contractors could submit bids at that scale, much less win them. They couldn't compete with the giants on labor availability, balance sheet strength, or track record.
Today, that landscape is changing. AI demand and an unprecedented wave of data center developments are stretching even the largest players. More firms are getting a chance to compete. The question for contractors is how to stand out once they are at the table.
One of the most overlooked advantages is the availability of tax incentives, particularly the federal Investment Tax Credit (ITC). In projects that include eligible energy property, the ITC can materially improve project economics. In an industry where
margins are tight
, and bids are often won by fractions of a percentage point, that matters.
Related:
Delivery Certainty Will Define the Next Phase of Data Center Growth
Where the Value Comes From
Power now sits at the center of every data center project. Developers are under pressure to meet rising energy demand while keeping long-term costs under control. As a result, more projects are investing in on-site solar,
battery storage
, microgrids, and other systems built for resilience. These assets may qualify for federal incentives, including the ITC.
One of us spent years inside the IRS helping shape how the agency administered the ITC. The detail that surprises many contractors is that the credit is not simply a fixed rate applied at the end of a project. It is designed to stack, and its value can change substantially based on decisions made throughout development and construction.
Where materials are sourced, how labor is structured, whether prevailing wage and apprenticeship requirements are satisfied, and how compliance is documented can all affect the size of the credit. Many of those decisions sit with the contractor.
Why Timing Matters
When contractors hear the word
credit," many assume it is a matter for the owner's finance team or tax advisors to figure out long after construction is completed. That assumption leaves value on the table.
Here's the thing most advisors don't tell you: by the time construction is finished, the best opportunities have usually passed. If sourcing is locked, labor plans are set, and the schedule was built without compliance in mind, the opportunity to maximize the ITC may be sharply reduced.
Related:
The AI Data Center Boom Is Here. Can Contractor Safety Keep Pace?
Contractors who plan for the credit from the start can flag sourcing and labor choices that affect eligibility and size. They can build prevailing wage and apprenticeship requirements into the budget and set up documentation early, so the record will stand up to review. In doing so, the value they can deliver to a client can climb from 6% to as much as 60%.
How the ITC Can Help Contractors Win a Bid
Submitting a bid with an ITC strategy takes less tax expertise than many contractors expect. Contractors do not need to become tax experts. They need enough working knowledge to spot opportunities, ask good questions, and invite the right specialists at the right time. That is a realistic goal for a mid-sized firm, and it starts with the first planning conversation.
Many of your competitors can build. Fewer can show an owner how to capture more value from the same project by aligning
construction planning
with the economics of eligible energy investments. For contractors looking to break into or move up in the data center sector, the Investment Tax Credit may be one of the smartest ways to win.
Related:
The Case For Pragmatism in the AI Infrastructure Boom

title: BNZ nears completion of 216 MWh of battery storage in Italy - Energy Storage
content: BNZ has started setting up BESS at its Rinaldone and Camposcala solar plants in Italy’s Lazio region. Both projects will integrate batteries into existing solar facilities operated by the company. The Rinaldone solar plant has an installed capacity of 45 MW, while Camposcala has 53 MW. Each new battery system will have a power output of 27 MW, an energy storage capacity of 108 MWh and a four-hour discharge duration. BNZ has also recently introduced a flock of 350 sheep and three shepherd dogs at the two solar plants. pv magazine Italia: Construction of the BESS at Rinaldone and Camposcala has started. What is the timeline? What are the different stages, and what work is currently underway? BNZ: Construction of the Rinaldone and Camposcala battery storage systems officially began in the third quarter of 2026. Each project involves integrating a 27 MW/108 MWh battery system, with a four-hour discharge duration, into our existing solar plants, which have capacities of 45 MWp at Rinaldone and 53 MWp at Camposcala, respectively. Our target is to achieve commercial operation by the end of 2026. All major equipment has already been delivered to the sites. We are currently focusing on electrical connections, system integration, testing and commissioning, while completing the final administrative requirements and grid connection procedures in parallel. If commissioning is scheduled for the end of the year, does that mean a battery storage system can be installed in less than two months? Not exactly. Although commissioning is scheduled for the end of the year, the projects are now in the final stages of construction, rather than at the beginning of the process. The battery containers and main equipment have already been delivered and installed at both sites. Our teams are now focusing on the remaining technical work, including electrical interconnections, system integration and testing, as well as completing the necessary administrative requirements and grid connection procedures. Why did you choose a four-hour duration? The four-hour discharge duration was selected following an in-depth internal assessment by our technical and revenue management teams, supported by external technical and market experts. We concluded that, for these specific projects, this configuration offers the best balance between grid flexibility, revenue generation, investment efficiency and long-term value creation. Do these two systems qualify for any incentive scheme? If so, which one? These systems do not currently benefit from any incentive mechanism. However, they could potentially qualify for new mechanisms introduced in the future. You have said that, during the development and construction phases, priority was given to involving local companies and workers, directly supporting economic activity and job creation in the region. This is an area where solar installations are increasing rapidly and where several stakeholders have raised concerns about a photovoltaic problem. Do you think this local approach can help limit opposition from communities? Can you provide any data or figures? We believe that involving local companies and workers helps foster positive relationships with the communities hosting our plants, while generating direct economic benefits. In addition, these BESS projects are being built within the boundaries of existing solar plants already operated by BNZ, minimizing any additional impact on the surrounding area. From the outset, our priority has been to integrate the projects into their local contexts as effectively as possible, creating shared value and limiting disruption. This approach is essential to building strong relationships with stakeholders and ensuring long-term project acceptance. As I understand it, BNZ plans to install 350 MW of battery storage capacity across a portfolio of eight strategic projects concentrated in areas with high solar irradiation in Italy. By when? BNZ’s current target is to reach approximately 350 MW of installed battery storage power in Italy by early 2028, corresponding to around 1.4 GWh of storage capacity. The Rinaldone and Camposcala projects represent the first phase of this strategy. The other projects will be developed progressively over the coming months and years as part of our broader plan to deploy battery storage systems across Italy. title: Captona and Sunrun announce financial partnership, supporting 110 MWh across 9,400 residential installs - Energy Storage
content: New York-based investment firm Captona has announced a preferred equity investment in Sunrun to support the residential installer’s project financing needs. While specific financial terms and portfolio capacities were not immediately disclosed, the parties said the deal would support 74 MW of solar and 110 MWh of battery storage across 9,400 residential installations in more than 20 states. In solar project finance, preferred equity allows a company like Sunrun to access flexible capital over a defined term while offering the investor a prioritized return compared to common shareholders. For Captona, the investment in Sunrun follows an earlier preferred equity transaction with community solar developer Nexamp. First announced in Oct. 2026, the firm said its investment would support 55 MW of solar generation and 5 MWh of battery storage capacity across 10 Nexamp projects in four states. “Our partnership with Sunrun marks the next chapter in Captona’s evolution as a premier investment partner in the energy transition,” said Captona founder and CEO Izzet Bensusan, in a statement. “We’re proud to work alongside one of the largest companies in the sector as we continue to grow and scale our business, expand our investment portfolio and build on the relationships we’ve established with industry leaders.” News of the investment comes shortly after Sunrun’s recent Q3 earnings report , in which the company revealed a 51.7% growth in revenue over the same quarter in 2025, largely on the strength of a separate financing transaction that sees the company selling many of the installations it initiates directly to a third party upon completion, allowing Sunrun to generate revenue from sales even as it maintains a long-term operating (and up-selling) relationship with the systems’ users. Since its inception in 2007, Sunrun has raised capital from a number of sources, historically depending on a mix of traditional debt and tax equity to finance the installation of its residential systems. The addition of preferred equity from partners like Captona gives Sunrun another way to raise capital outside of its standard tax equity partnerships and senior debt facilities. title: Delta advances 400 MW/800 MWh battery project in Australia - Energy Storage
content: Delta Electricity, owned by Czech company Sev.en Global Investments, has lodged a development application and environmental impact statement (EIS) for a large-scale battery energy storage system (BESS) to be built at the site of the Vales Point power station in the New South Wales (NSW) Hunter region. Developed in partnership with South Korean industrial giant Samsung C&T , the proposed BESS will provide up to 400 MW/800 MWh energy storage capacity. Delta said once operational, the Vales Point BESS will operate 24/7 to help strengthen grid reliability and support renewable energy generation as part of the region’s evolving role in NSW’s energy transition “Australia’s energy mix and landscape is changing significantly and this project will be a key part of this change,” the company said. “The battery will support the energy transition by strengthening the grid, improving energy reliability and helping manage the significant supply volatility created by an energy system dominated by variable renewable energy.” The Vales Point battery will take advantage of existing grid infrastructure with Delta noting the site is “uniquely positioned” to participate in the energy transition after the coal-fired units are closed. The site is a hub for transmission infrastructure and located within the Hunter-Central Coast Renewable Energy Zone , which is expected to deliver 1 GW of additional network transfer capacity by 2028. The State Significant Development Application (SSDA) and supporting EIS for the proposed Vales Point BESS have now been lodged with the NSW Department of Planning, Housing and Infrastructure for assessment. Delta said the submission follows 18 months of “extensive technical and environmental studies” and is a major step forward for the project. The proposed Vales Point BESS reflects a broader shift among utilities toward pairing generation assets with battery capacity as the grid transitions away from coal-fired baseload power. It follows other coal plant operators also choosing battery energy storage, including the nearby 850 MW/1,680 MWh Waratah Super Battery , the AGL Energy-owned 500 MW/1,000 MWh Liddell BESS, and Origin Energy’s Eraring battery that will ultimately deliver a facility rated at 1,200 MW/8,600 MWh. EnergyAustralia also has plans to install a 500 MW/2,000 MWh BESS adjacent to its Mt Piper coal-fired power station in NSW’s central west. Other projects include the 150 MW/150 MWh BESS built at the site of retired coal-fired Hazelwood power station in Victoria’s Latrobe Valley, and the 300 MW/600 MWh Tarong and 300 MW/1,200 MWh Stanwell batteries in Queensland. Delta has announced it will shut down the Vales Point power station in 2033. The 1,320 MW plant provides about 4% of Australia’s electricity needs. title: German utility plans 30 MWh zinc-bromine BESS from Eos, aiming at long-term value - Energy Storage
content: Stadtwerke Gaggenau, the municipal utility of southwest German town Gaggenau, and German energy infrastructure company Capac AG are planning a stackable, large-scale battery energy storage system (BESS) based on zinc-bromide technology. Construction of the 7.5 MW/30 MWh system, which will be built on the former site of the utility’s liquefied gas plant, is set to begin next year. Capac is acting as general contractor, handling the technical planning, procurement, system integration and construction up to commissioning, which is planned for 2028. Benjamin Henecka, CEO of Capac Energy, told ESS News the main benefit of zinc-bromine technology is the combination of a non-flammable, water-based electrolyte, a long expected operating life and low projected capacity degradation. “The zinc-bromine battery technology is designed for a 25-year operating life with capacity degradation of around 3.6% over that period,” Henecka explained. “These characteristics make it an attractive option for utilities taking a long-term infrastructure investment approach. The safety case is also critical as there is no thermal runaway and the water-based electrolyte is non-flammable.” Long-term infrastructure cost focus Stadtwerke Gaggenau and investment company JP Holding, parent company of Capac, are jointly investing €15.2 million ($16.8 million) in the project. Henecka said that from the companies’ perspective, the economic question is not simply which battery has the lowest purchase price but also which system delivers the required storage service most economically over the full investment period. “A higher initial investment can be justified by low capacity degradation and a reduced need for subsequent capacity additions or replacements,” he explained. “That comparison must also account for auxiliary consumption, maintenance and financing costs under the same operating profile. Our argument is about lifecycle value, not a claim that zinc-bromine wins on every individual metric.” Henecka added that the project is structured as a long-term infrastructure investment. Its planned revenue sources include arbitrage trading in the day-ahead and intraday markets, alongside additional ancillary services. The zinc-bromine BESS will be built using battery systems supplied by US manufacturer Eos. Eos’ Intensity architecture uses modular battery units installed within an engineered steel support structure that allows units to be arranged both horizontally and vertically. Its zinc-based batteries, manufactured in Pennsylvania, use materials including zinc bromide, conductive plastic and graphite felt. “The non-flammable aqueous chemistry is an important enabler of this compact layout,” Henecka added. “Together with the system’s protective controls and physical design, it provides a different fire-risk profile from conventional lithium-ion systems.” Henecka told ESS News the partnership offers a practical way to reduce exposure to Chinese-dominated lithium-ion supply chains. “It is not about replacing one dependency with another or claiming complete supply-chain independence. It is about giving European utilities a broader choice of technologies and suppliers, reducing concentration risk and strengthening their ability to respond to changing market conditions,” he explained. “We combine that alternative technology with local engineering, system integration and long-term operational support.” In June, Capac and Eos unveiled plans for a 5 MW/22 MWh zinc-bromine battery project in the German city of Bruchsal. At the time, they also announced a deal covering 2 GWh of storage capacity across Germany, Austria and Switzerland through 2031. title: Helleniq Energy plans €1 billion outlay for BESS and renewables portfolio in Romania - Energy Storage
content: Greek energy group Helleniq Energy has announced plans to invest more than €1 billion in Romania by 2030, targeting a significant portfolio expansion. Through its subsidiary Helleniq Renewables, it is developing a portfolio of solar, wind, and battery energy storage system (BESS) projects in the country, with Romania set to become the company’s second-most important renewables growth market after Greece.  It aims to establish a “production and storage portfolio” of up to 1.3 GW in Romania. Helleniq Renewables said its Romanian portfolio exceeds 800 MW of renewable energy capacity and 500 MW of BESS, including operational assets, projects under construction and a development pipeline. The company presented the investment and development program at an event held in Bucharest on November 9, which it said marked the official launch of Helleniq Renewables Romania. The Helleniq Renewables Romania portfolio currently consists of four solar photovoltaic (PV) parks with a combined installed capacity of 211 MW in Teleorman, Giurgiu, Olt and Dolj counties. The company is also developing a 96 MW wind farm in Galați County, which is scheduled for completion in Q2 2027. The broader pipeline includes more than 500 MW of renewable energy projects and 500 MW of BESS capacity. Deputy CEO George Alexopoulos said Helleniq Energy expects to have 500 MW of battery storage capacity in operation in Romania by 2030. “Romania is a strategic market for Helleniq Energy and a key part of our long-term growth plans in Southeast Europe. Our commitment to invest over €1 billion by 2030 by establishing a production and storage portfolio of up to 1.3 GW reflects our confidence in the country’s potential and our ambition to establish a strong and lasting presence in its energy sector,” said Andreas Shiamishis, CEO of Helleniq Energy. Across five countries, Helleniq Energy said it manages a renewable energy project portfolio exceeding 6 GW, with more than 800 MW already operational. The company is targeting more than 2 GW of installed renewable capacity by 2030 and expects total investments to exceed €2 billion. Last month, Helleniq Renewables completed the construction of the 100 MW / 200 MWh Thessaloniki BESS . title: Genesis reveals GV90 prices start at $100K+ in Korea, but it will cost more for coach doors
content:
Peter Johnson
| Nov 11 2026 - 6:22 am PT
opened orders for the ultra-luxury electric SUV in South Korea, with prices starting at over $100,000. If you want coach doors, however, it will cost you a bit more.
Genesis GV90 prices and driving range in Korea
Hyundai’s luxury brand is moving upscale with the GV90, its first fully electric three-row flagship SUV.
After unveiling the GV90 at the Palace of Fine Arts in San Francisco in August (
which we had the pleasure to see firsthand
), Genesis launched the new “ultra-luxe” SUV in its home market of Korea on Tuesday.
The Genesis GV90 introduces several “world-first” innovations, including the first independently opening and closing B-pillarless coach doors, a 12-airbag roof airbag system, and genuine wood floors with radiant heating.
It’s available in two models: the GV90 Standard with traditional swing doors and the GV90 Neolun, which features the “Neolun Arch Gate,” Genesis’ hidden B-pillar coach door system.
In Korea, the Genesis GV90 Standard 7-seater model starts at 139.5 million won, or about $104,000.
Genesis GV90 Neolun (Source: Peter Johnson/ Electrek)
The GV90 Individual Lounge Seat (6-seater) starts at 145.5 million won ($108,500); the GV90 Neolun Standard (6-seater) starts at 189.9 million won ($141,500), while the top-spec GV90 Neolun Executive Suite (4-seater) starts at 239.5 million won ($178,500).
Based on Hyundai’s new eMP platform, developed exclusively for its flagships, Genesis said the GV90 is like a “moving private lounge,” complete with a multi-chamber air suspension and a dual electronic limited-slip differential (E-LSD).

Genesis GV90 price by trim in South Korea
A luxury private lounge on wheels
The platform is designed to open up interior space for the B-pillarless coach doors, swivel seats, and more.
When parked, the front seats swivel a full 180 degrees to face rear passengers or to create what Genesis calls “a face-to-face lounge-like configuration.”
The interior is about as over-the-top as you could expect, with massive digital screens, premium materials, and plenty of luxury extras.
The GV90 is the first Hyundai Motor Group vehicle to feature its new extendable display and the first Genesis model equipped with its next-gen Pleos Connect infotainment system.
Together, they create what Genesis calls a new realm of “display expandability.” While other vehicles, like the new Tucson and IONIQ 3, also use Pleos Connect, Hyundai developed an exclusive version for the GV90.
Genesis GV90 Neolun infotainment display (Source: Peter Johnson/ Electrek)
When the vehicle is parked, the screen can expand to 24.6″ at the push of a button, transforming it into a massive Cinematic Display.
Once extended, the display switches to Media Home mode, where you can watch Netflix, live TV, stream music, and more with third-party apps.
A mobile private theater wouldn’t be complete without a premium audio system, right? To top it off, Genesis added a 25-speaker Bang & Olufsen Premier 3D Sound System with Dolby Atmos, so it sounds like you’re actually at the movies.
In place of a traditional instrument cluster, the GV90 has a 25″ Head-Up Display (HUD) that shows the vehicle’s speed, navigation directions, and other ADAS functions directly on the windshield.
The GV90 is also the first Hyundai Motor Group vehicle with a buttonless power system. When you enter the vehicle and close the door, the Motion Column Shifter moves from the 12 o’clock position to the 2 o’clock position.
Meanwhile, the Crystal Sphere between the driver and passenger rotates to indicate it’s ready to drive. The vehicle starts when you press the brake.
Genesis GV90 debut (Source: Peter Johnson/ Electrek)
Dimensions, battery size, other specs
As a full-size flagship SUV, the Genesis GV90 is massive. It measures 208.1″ (5,285 mm) long, 79.9″ (2,030 mm) wide, and 71.5″ (1,815 mm) tall (71.4″ with 24″ tires), with a 127.8″ (3,245 mm) wheelbase.
That’s even bigger than the Hyundai IONIQ 9 (199.2″/5,060 mm in length) and Kia EV9 (197.4″/5,010 mm).
To power a full-size flagship SUV, it needs a big battery. The GV90 uses a 123.5 kWh battery, the largest among Hyundai Motor’s EVs, which Genesis said provides a driving range of 500 km (310 miles) for the 7-seater version with 22″ wheels.
The GV90 Neonlun 6-seater with 24″ wheels has a range of up to 460 km (286 miles) on a single charge.
It’s equipped with a new dual-motor all-wheel-drive (AWD) system that delivers a combined 657 hp (490 kW) and 590 lb-ft (800 Nm) of torque, making it Hyundai Motor Group’s most powerful electric vehicle.
When using a 350 kW fast charger, the vehicle’s battery can recharge from 10% to 80% in about 22 minutes.
Genesis GV90 Neolun (left) GV90 Neolun First Edition (middle) and GV90 (right) Source: Hyundai
“Thanks to the enthusiastic interest and support for the GV90 since its global premiere, we have begun full-scale sales in Korea first,” a Genesis official said, adding the flagship SUV will “set a new standard for luxury.”
Following Korea, Genesis is expected to launch the GV90 in the US and other global markets in early 2027.
Genesis has yet to reveal US prices, but the GV90 Standard model is expected to start at around $100,000. The GV90 Neolun, on the other hand, will likely start closer to $150,000 or more.
What do you think of the flagship Genesis GV90? Would you buy the standard version for about $100,000 or pay the extra for the Neolun with coach doors? Let us know in the comments.

title: It’s that time again – Honda needs to roll out an electric Super Cub
content:
Electric Motorcycles
Micah Toll
| Nov 11 2026 - 3:40 am PT
Every few years, I apparently feel compelled to remind Honda that it is sitting on what could be one of the easiest home runs in the electric motorcycle industry: just make an electric Super Cub already.
I’m not talking about an electric scooter vaguely inspired by the Super Cub. Not another futuristic concept with swoopy bodywork and a name that looks like a Wi-Fi password. I mean an actual honest-to-goodness Honda Super Cub, except electric.
The formula is already sitting right there.
The Honda Super Cub is arguably the most successful motor vehicle ever created,
with well over 100 million produced
since its introduction in 1958. It’s still in continuous production today.
And a huge part of that success comes down to how approachable the thing is. It isn’t supposed to be intimidating, excessively powerful, or particularly complicated. It’s simple, practical transportation wrapped in one of the most recognizable two-wheeler designs ever created.
In other words, it’s practically begging to become electric.
The beauty of the bike is how simple and timeless it is, with the appearance barely changing in nearly 7 decades. And with the design freedom that electric drivetrains provide, upgrading the cute little bike to an electric future would be a walk in the park for Honda’s engineers.
An in-wheel motor would be a simple, cheap solution that frees up even more space in the body for batteries.
And Honda wouldn’t need some enormous battery capable of highway touring. Give an electric Super Cub enough battery for perhaps 50-60 miles (80-95 km) of real-world urban riding, a motor capable of roughly 50-60 mph (80-95 km/h), and simple Level 1 charging from a normal wall outlet. As a city runabout or a beachside cruiser, those middle-of-the-road specs would be perfect.
Even better, make the battery removable. Honda already has its
Mobile Power Pack e: swappable battery system
used in various electric two-wheelers, and an electric Super Cub would be an incredible platform to expand it.
The resulting bike could hit an unusually sweet spot.
The Honda EV Cub concept
unveiled 10 years ago
and subsequently abandoned
There are millions of people riding electric bicycles today
who will eventually want something faster
, but don’t necessarily want a 500-pound (220 kg) electric motorcycle capable of hitting 120 mph (200 km/h). An electric Super Cub would be a natural next step: light, unintimidating, easy to ride, cheap to operate, and fast enough to actually function as a real urban vehicle.
It would also be one of the rare electric motorcycles that could appeal to people who aren’t necessarily looking for an “electric motorcycle.” An electric version is in such high demand that
companies specialize in retrofit kits
to convert classic Cubs into EVs.
The Super Cub already has decades of cultural cachet. It’s cute. It’s useful. It’s nostalgic without feeling ancient. It’s the kind of motorcycle that can appeal equally to a lifelong rider and someone who has never considered owning a motorcycle before.
And perhaps most importantly, Honda could actually sell the thing globally. The same basic electric Super Cub could work in dense European cities, throughout Asia, and in American cities and suburbs. It doesn’t need to win spec-sheet battles. It just needs to be affordable, reliable, and unmistakably a Super Cub.
Honda has already shown that it understands the importance of electrifying small two-wheelers. It’s even made a token gesture with a
Cub-like e-scooter in China
. But there’s a difference between making another electric scooter and electrifying perhaps the most famous small motorcycle ever made.
So here I am once again, Honda.
You’ve got the name. You’ve got the design. You’ve got the batteries. You’ve got the manufacturing scale.
Just put all the pieces together and give us the electric Super Cub already. The world is waiting, and will thank you.
